features.name: 1. Site and page configuration (window.SITE_CONFIG + window.PAGE)
features.what_it_does: Lets one app.js serve every industry page. config.js supplies the brand, the default agent ID, an optional webhook and default ROI assumptions. window.PAGE supplies the per-page words used in agent-facing strings, ROI constants, greetings, the agent context note and an optional per-page agent ID.
features.how_it_works: config.js is a classic script that sets window.SITE_CONFIG = { BRAND: 'Amariya', AGENT_ID: 'agent_9101m3n1hwxffey830jzf43chj6x', FORM_WEBHOOK_URL: '', ROI: { missedCallRate: 0.25, bookingConversion: 0.3, avgBookingValue: 220, minutesPerCall: 4 } }. build_pages.py emits an inline <script>window.PAGE = {...}</script>. Its value is {"industry": page.key, ...industries/<key>.json -> page}, JSON-escaped so '<' becomes <. Script order is: inline PAGE, then config.js (classic), then app.js and experience.js (type=module, so deferred), so both globals exist when app.js runs. app.js reads CONFIG = window.SITE_CONFIG || {}, PAGE = window.PAGE || {}, BRAND = CONFIG.BRAND || 'Amariya'. The build substitutes {brand}, {base} and {company} in every JSON string (fill_tokens). {part} is left for runtime. PAGE fields app.js reads: industry, agentId (no page sets it), sectionLabel, businessNoun, nameLabel, unitsPlural, unitEstimate, roi, greetings {evening, returning[], fresh[]}, agentContext.
dom_contract: window.SITE_CONFIG: read; set by config.js before the modules
window.PAGE: read; inline script emitted by build_pages.py

html.js: class added by an inline head script; CSS gates the split-text and pinned effects on it

features.name: 2. ElevenLabs SDK loading (version, import, warm-up)
features.what_it_does: Loads the ElevenLabs Agents browser SDK lazily and warms it shortly after page load, so pressing the orb connects quickly.
features.how_it_works: loadSdk() runs once and caches the result: ({ Conversation } = await import('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@elevenlabs/client@1.25.0/+esm')). On window 'load', a setTimeout of 800 ms calls loadSdk().catch(() => {}) as a silent warm-up; if it fails, start() tries again. Only Conversation.startSession(options) is used. I checked the npm package @elevenlabs/client@1.25.0 (published 2026-09-07; latest is 1.28.0 from 2026-10-13; dependencies livekit-client ^2.21.0 and @elevenlabs/types 0.23.0). startSession returns a TextConversation when textOnly is true and a VoiceConversation otherwise. Instance methods app.js calls all exist in 1.25.0: getId(), endSession(), setMicMuted(bool), sendUserMessage(text), sendUserActivity(), sendContextualUpdate(text, {contextId?}), getInputVolume(), getOutputVolume(). Callback payloads: onConnect({conversationId}); onDisconnect(details {reason: 'error'|'agent'|'user', ...}); onError(message, context?); onModeChange({mode: 'speaking'|'listening'}); onMessage({message, role: 'user'|'agent', source: 'user'|'ai' (deprecated), event_id?}).
dom_contract: (no DOM) Network: ESM import from cdn.jsdelivr.net; then ElevenLabs over WebRTC/LiveKit for voice or WebSocket for text-only
features.config_and_data: The version is pinned in the import URL (1.25.0).
features.port_notes: Install @elevenlabs/client at exactly 1.25.0, the version this code was written against, and load it with await import('@elevenlabs/client') so Vite puts it in its own chunk. It pulls in livekit-client, so keep it off the critical path. Keep the warm-up (idle or load + 800 ms) and also warm on pointerenter or focus of any talk control. Drop the CDN import. Available in 1.25.0 but unused, and useful for the new orbs and captions: getInputByteFrequencyData() and getOutputByteFrequencyData() (per-band audio for shaders), onVadScore, onInterruption, onAudioAlignment (word timing for synced captions), onAgentChatResponsePart (streaming text), onStatusChange, onAgentTyping, setVolume. If a Content Security Policy is added, AudioWorkletConfig.workletPaths lets you self-host the audio worklets instead of allowing blob: and data:.

features.name: 3. Start flow and the pre-call sheet (dialog)
features.what_it_does: Pressing a talk control while idle first opens a one-time explainer ('Say hello to Amariya') before the browser's mic prompt. The visitor picks 'Start with voice' or 'Type instead', or closes it. Text entry points skip the sheet. If no agent ID is configured, a toast appears instead.
features.how_it_works: requestStart(preferred) works in this order. - If CONFIG.AGENT_ID is missing or equals 'YOUR_AGENT_ID': toast 'Add your ElevenLabs agent ID in config.js to enable voice.' and stop. Only CONFIG is checked, not PAGE.agentId. - preferred === 'text': start('text') directly, without the sheet. - sheetSeen (module variable, per page load): start('voice'). - Otherwise: sheet.returnValue = ''; sheet.showModal(). A one-time 'close' listener checks the returnValue: 'voice' or 'text' sets sheetSeen = true and calls start(returnValue). 'cancel' or Esc does nothing, and the sheet shows again next time. Sheet copy: - h3#sheet-title: 'Say hello to {brand}'. - First item: 'A quick chat, about 3 minutes. {sheet.ask}' (e.g. "She'll ask about your hotel and walk you through the site as you talk."). - Second item: 'Uses your microphone. Your browser will ask for permission. You can mute or switch to typing any time.' - Third item: 'Interrupt her whenever you like, just like a normal conversation.' - Buttons: 'Start with voice' (mic icon, autofocus) and 'Type instead'; a close button with aria-label 'Close'. Controls that lead here: - .js-talk: the hero orb button, the hero 'Talk to {brand}' button, the footer 'Talk to {brand}' button and the dock orb. - .js-type: the hero 'Chat by text' button. - Hero note: 'About 3 minutes · switch to typing any time · or just browse'.

features.name: 4. Session start: startSession options, agent ID resolution, first message, context note
features.what_it_does: Opens a voice (WebRTC) or text-only conversation with the agent, personalised for the page and the visit, then sends the agent a note on the page's industry.
features.how_it_works:
start(chosen) does the following.
1. mode = chosen; thread.innerHTML = '' (each session starts a fresh transcript); setState('connecting').
2. Caption: voice 'Allow microphone access to talk with {BRAND}…'; text 'Opening the chat…'.
3. Voice only: await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({audio:true}) as a permission check.
4. SDK = await loadSdk(); ctx = visitContext().
5. conversation = await SDK.startSession({ agentId: PAGE.agentId || CONFIG.AGENT_ID, ...(voice ? {connectionType:'webrtc'} : {textOnly:true}), dynamicVariables: ctx.dynamicVariables, overrides: { agent: { firstMessage: pickGreeting(ctx) }, tts: ctx.tts }, clientTools, onConnect, onDisconnect: () => stopUi(), onError, onModeChange, onMessage }).
6. Once it resolves: if PAGE.agentContext exists, contextUpdate(PAGE.agentContext). This is a stopgap so the one shared hotel agent knows its name, the page's industry, what each profile field, feature key and plan means on this page, and (on clinic pages) never to give medical advice.
Callbacks:
- onConnect: chime(); setState('thinking'); caption('{BRAND} is joining…'); showTyping(). In text mode also openPanel(true) and focus #typeForm [name=msg].
- onError(err): console.error, then toast 'Connection hiccup — please try again.' The state is not changed.
dom_contract: #typeForm input[name=msg]: focused when a text session connects
features.config_and_data:
Agent ID: PAGE.agentId || CONFIG.AGENT_ID (today always agent_9101m3n1hwxffey830jzf43chj6x). The overrides used need 'First message', 'TTS speed' and 'TTS stability' overrides enabled on the agent; AGENT_SETUP says they are. agentContext text by file:
- hotels.json line 126: 'Your name is {brand}. Always introduce and refer to yourself as {brand}, never by any other name. The visitor is on the page for hotels.'
- aesthetics.json, dental.json and home.json line 125: long notes mapping the hotel-named fields, feature keys and plans to the industry, plus the safety rule.
features.port_notes: Keep the SessionConfig option names exactly as in SDK 1.25.0: agentId, connectionType ('webrtc'|'websocket'), textOnly, dynamicVariables, overrides.agent.firstMessage, overrides.tts.speed and overrides.tts.stability. A new override (overrides.agent.language, prompt or a voice ID) is refused unless it is enabled on the agent first. Always send all three dynamic variables: the session is refused if the agent's prompt uses a variable that is not supplied. Keep sending agentContext right after connect until each niche has its own agent (AGENT_SETUP step 3). Add every Astro dev, preview and production host to the agent's allowlist, or startSession fails with "Host … is not allowed to connect to this agent". Guard against a double start: today only the .js-talk handler ignores clicks while connecting.

features.name: 5. Visit context: dynamic variables and per-visit voice pace
features.what_it_does: Adjusts the agent's tone, pace and greeting to the time of day, to whether this browser has talked to her before, and to the device.
features.how_it_works:
visitContext() is called only inside start().
- returning = !!localStorage.getItem('aria_visited'), then localStorage.setItem('aria_visited', '1'), both in try/catch. So 'returning' means 'has started a conversation before in this browser'; a second call in the same page load already counts.
- h = new Date().getHours(); part = h < 12 ? 'morning' : h < 18 ? 'afternoon' : 'evening'. 00:00-11:59 is 'morning', including the small hours.
- mobile = matchMedia('(max-width: 700px), (pointer: coarse)').matches.
- pace = {morning: 1.04, afternoon: 1.0, evening: 0.95}[part] + (mobile ? 0.02 : 0); jitter(r) = (Math.random()*2 - 1)*r.
- It returns { part, returning, dynamicVariables: { time_of_day: part, visitor_status: returning ? 'returning' : 'new', visitor_device: mobile ? 'mobile' : 'desktop' }, tts: { speed: +(pace + jitter(0.02)).toFixed(2), stability: +(0.3 + jitter(0.04)).toFixed(2) } }.
features.config_and_data: The value sets time_of_day (morning/afternoon/evening), visitor_status (new/returning) and visitor_device (mobile/desktop) are the ones the agent prompt's 'Tone & energy' section expects. TTS speed range is about 0.93-1.08; stability is 0.26-0.34.
features.port_notes: Keep the value sets exactly. Adding 'night' (21:00-05:59, matching experience.js, where night = h >= 21 || h < 6) would suit the hotel night story, but the prompt must be updated first. The new site is a new origin, so every visitor starts as 'new', and the key can be renamed (e.g. amariya_visited) without loss. Keep the try/catch around storage (private browsing).

features.name: 6. Greetings (overrides.agent.firstMessage per page)
features.what_it_does: Varies the agent's first line per visit: an evening line, 'welcome back' lines for returning visitors, or one of several fresh greetings. Each says she is an AI receptionist for that industry and asks the business name.
features.how_it_works: pickGreeting({part, returning}) reads g = PAGE.greetings. When it exists: line = (part === 'evening' && !returning && Math.random() < 0.5) ? g.evening : pick(returning ? g.returning : g.fresh), then returns line.replaceAll('{part}', part). Without PAGE.greetings, app.js falls back to hard-coded hotel lines (lines 528-542). The lines contain ElevenLabs v3 audio tags such as [warmly], [laughs softly] and [curious], which the voice performs and the transcript strips. Per page there are 1 evening and 2 returning lines; hotels has 4 fresh lines, aesthetics, dental and home have 3.
features.config_and_data: industries/<page>.json -> page.greetings {evening: string, returning: string[], fresh: string[]}. {brand} is already substituted; {part} is substituted at runtime.
features.port_notes: Copy the greeting sets per niche, rewriting for restaurants (hotels niche) and physicians (clinics niche). Keep the AI disclosure in every line (the identity rule in AGENT_SETUP). The hotel fallback in app.js becomes unnecessary once every niche has greetings. The first-message override must stay enabled on each agent.

features.name: 7. Microphone permission and error handling
features.what_it_does: Asks for the mic with a caption, switches to text chat if the visitor refuses, and shows short toasts for other failures.
features.how_it_works:
In start('voice'), the caption reads 'Allow microphone access to talk with {BRAND}…', then await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({audio:true}) runs before the SDK loads. Any error thrown in start(): console.error; stopUi(); then:
- err.name === 'NotAllowedError': toast 'No microphone access — switching to text chat.' and return start('text').
- Anything else: toast "Couldn't start the conversation. Please try again."
Errors during a session go to onError and show the toast 'Connection hiccup — please try again.'
Mute: #muteBtn calls conversation.setMicMuted(muted).
features.config_and_data: The microphone needs https:// or localhost (AGENT_SETUP section 6).
features.port_notes:
Bugs to fix in the port:
1. The permission-check stream is never stopped. Call stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()) once permission is granted, or the browser's mic-in-use indicator can stay on after the call ends.
2. Only NotAllowedError falls back to text. Also fall back on NotFoundError (no mic), NotReadableError (mic in use), SecurityError, and a missing navigator.mediaDevices (insecure origin, which today throws a TypeError and shows the generic toast).
3. Allowlist rejections only show the generic toast; give them a clearer message.
Show the permission state in each concept's own UI, not only in the one-line caption.

features.name: 8. Conversation state machine, status copy and orb label
features.what_it_does: One shared state drives the dock, the hero orb label, the orbs and the CSS. States: idle, connecting, thinking, listening, speaking. Modes: voice or text. The muted flag adjusts the copy.
features.how_it_works:
setState(state):
- Writes dock.dataset.state = state, dock.dataset.mode = mode and document.body.dataset.state = state.
- [data-status] text: 'Mic muted' if muted and listening; 'Your turn' in text mode while listening; otherwise STATUS[state]. STATUS = {idle: '{BRAND} is ready to talk', connecting: 'Connecting', listening: 'Listening', thinking: 'Thinking', speaking: '{BRAND} is speaking'}.
- [data-orb-label]: idle 'Tap to talk', connecting 'Connecting…', any other state 'Tap to end'.
- [data-live-only] is hidden while idle or connecting; #muteBtn is hidden in text mode.
Transitions:
- Page load: idle. start(): connecting. onConnect: thinking, with typing dots.
- Voice, onModeChange 'speaking': remove the typing dots and switch to speaking.
- Voice, onModeChange 'listening': switch to listening unless the state is thinking (it stays thinking until she speaks).
- onMessage from the user (voice transcript): thinking, with typing dots.
- onMessage from the agent while thinking: speaking in voice mode, listening in text mode.
- Text mode ignores onModeChange. A typed message sets thinking with typing dots; the agent's reply sets listening ('Your turn').
- stop() or a disconnect: idle. Toggling mute re-runs setState with the current state to refresh the copy.
dom_contract: CSS (styles.css): [data-state=listening] .hero-orb-label sets border mint, [data-state=speaking] sets border warm (135-136)
CSS: .dock[data-state=speaking|listening] border colours (528-529); [data-state=listening|speaking] .dock-status colour (534-535); [data-state=thinking] .dock-status::after animated dots (545-546)

experience.js reads body.dataset.state every frame and blends connecting/listening/thinking/speaking weights (k = min(1, dt*4)). On the hero sphere, thinking adds +0.5 and connecting +0.8 to rotation speed.
features.config_and_data: Copy strings as listed. BRAND comes from config.
features.port_notes: The new OrbStage (amariya/src/scripts/orb/stage.ts) only knows 'idle' | 'listening' | 'speaking', and it ignores the voice level unless speaking. Extend OrbState with 'connecting' and 'thinking' (or map them on purpose), and add a tone input. Keep body/dock data-state as a public hook so each concept's CSS can react. New hard constraint: the orb status must sit in a polite live region, and today [data-status] is not one. Announce the changes that matter (connecting, connected, muted, ended), not every listening/speaking flip.

features.name: 9. Emotional tone from audio tags, and tag stripping
features.what_it_does: Tints the orb to the emotion of the agent's current line (bright, soft, calm, warm) and keeps audio tags out of captions and the transcript.
features.how_it_works: setTone(raw) takes the first tag matching /\[([^\]]{1,32})\]/ and lowercases it. TONES = {excited: 'bright', playfully: 'bright', 'laughs softly': 'bright', softly: 'soft', sighs: 'soft', thoughtful: 'soft', reassuring: 'calm', warmly: 'warm', curious: 'warm'}; anything else, including no tag, gives 'warm'. It writes dock.dataset.tone and body.dataset.tone, and runs on every agent message before cleaning. clean(t) removes every /\[[^\]]{1,32}\]\s*/g, collapses double spaces and trims.
dom_contract: CSS: [data-tone=bright][data-state=speaking] .orb {filter: saturate(1.3) brightness(1.1)}; soft {saturate(.75) brightness(.92)}; calm {hue-rotate(-14deg) saturate(.9)}
experience.js TONE_BRIGHT = {bright: 1.15, soft: 0.85, calm: 0.95}, a brightness multiplier applied only while speaking
features.config_and_data: The agent's 10 suggested audio tags (AGENT_SETUP): excited, warmly, softly, curious, laughs softly, sighs, thoughtful, playfully, reassuring, short pause ('short pause' maps to warm).
features.port_notes: Keep TONES and clean() as they are. Feed the tone into the new orb shaders (core glow, colour temperature, rim strength) instead of CSS filters on the canvas.

features.name: 10. Dock: the persistent live-call bar and its controls
features.what_it_does: A bar fixed to the bottom of every page. It holds a mini orb (start/end), a status line with a 5-bar level meter, a one-line caption of the latest utterance, and live-only actions: transcript, mute, end. It expands into the conversation panel.
features.how_it_works:
Markup: aside#dock.dock[data-state=idle][aria-label='Conversation with {brand}'] contains:
- div#panel.panel[hidden]: header 'Conversation' with #collapseBtn, ol#thread, form#typeForm.
- div.dock-bar: button.dock-orb.js-talk[aria-label='Start or end conversation'] holding span.orb.orb-sm[data-orb]; div.dock-body with p.dock-status (span[data-status] + span.wave of 5 <i>) and p.dock-caption[data-caption] ('Press the orb and say hello.'); div.dock-actions[data-live-only][hidden] with #transcriptBtn, #muteBtn (svg.ico-mic + svg.ico-mic-off) and #endBtn.icon-end.
Behaviour:
- .js-talk click: idle calls requestStart('voice'); connecting is ignored; any live state calls stop(), which also ends a text chat.
- .js-type: idle calls requestStart('text'); otherwise openPanel(true).
- #endBtn calls stop(); #transcriptBtn calls openPanel(panel.hidden); #collapseBtn calls openPanel(false).
- Esc (window keydown) closes the panel when it is open and the start sheet is not.
- #muteBtn: muted = !muted; conversation?.setMicMuted(muted); updates aria-pressed and aria-label ('Unmute microphone' or 'Mute microphone'); then setState(current state).
- openPanel(open): panel.hidden = !open; toggles #dock.expanded; sets #transcriptBtn aria-expanded and aria-label ('Hide conversation' or 'Show conversation'); scrolls the thread to the bottom.
- caption(text, who): adds .swap (opacity 0); after 120 ms sets textContent and title (the full text as a tooltip, since the caption is one line with ellipsis), toggles .user, removes .swap.
Layout: centred; width min(540px, 100% - 32px); bottom 16px plus the safe area; z-index 30. At 900px and wider, the expanded dock moves right (right: 24px, width 400px). At 600px and narrower: width 100% - 16px, bottom 8px.
dom_contract: CSS: .icon-btn[aria-pressed=true] swaps the mic icons and tints red; .icon-btn[aria-expanded=true] is filled; .dock-caption.user is mint; .dock-caption.swap has opacity 0

features.port_notes: The old bottom dock ('Amariya is ready to talk — Press the orb and say hello') is a signature element. Each concept can reinvent it, but must keep: start and end from anywhere, live status in a live region, the last utterance as a caption, access to the transcript, mute (voice only), end, Esc to collapse, and targets of at least 44px (the icon buttons are 40px today). features.name: 11. Transcript thread, typing indicator, activity lines, text chat composer
features.what_it_does: The panel shows the conversation as bubbles (agent left, visitor right), three bouncing dots while she thinks, and small centred 'activity' lines when she changes the page. Visitors can type in both text and voice sessions.
features.how_it_works:
addMsg(role, text): removes the typing dots, appends li.msg.{ai|user} with textContent, scrolls to the bottom.
showTyping(): only one at a time; li.msg.ai.typing[aria-label='{BRAND} is thinking'] containing three <i>.
activity(text): appends li.msg.activity, placed before the typing dots if they are showing.
onMessage adds the cleaned text as a bubble and as the caption; the visitor's captions get the prefix 'You: '.
#typeForm submit (preventDefault): text = msg.value.trim(); requires a live conversation; conversation.sendUserMessage(text); addMsg('user'); caption('You: …', 'user'); setState('thinking'); showTyping(); clear the input.

Activity lines: 'Updated your {businessNoun} profile', 'Calculated your estimate', 'Recommended the {plan} plan', 'Filled in your demo details', 'Demo request sent'.

features.config_and_data: BRAND, PAGE.businessNoun
features.port_notes: Keep data-lenis-prevent (or Lenis's prevent option) on the scrollable thread, and keep aria-live=polite. Add dir='auto' to the bubbles; today Arabic and other right-to-left lines render left-to-right. The code assumes the SDK does not echo typed messages back through onMessage. Check this with 1.25.0 text sessions and remove duplicates if it does. Keep 'Chat by text' behaviour (no sheet, no mic) under each concept's own copy.

features.name: 12. Audio-reactive level loop (--level) and the orb hooks
features.what_it_does: Makes the orbs and the 5-bar meter pulse with her voice while she speaks and with the visitor's mic while listening.
features.how_it_works:
levelEls = every [data-orb] plus .wave. On every animation frame: if there is a conversation in voice mode, level = state 'speaking' ? conversation.getOutputVolume() : (state 'listening' and not muted) ? conversation.getInputVolume() : 0; otherwise 0. Then smooth += (min(1, level*2.2) - smooth) * 0.35, and each element gets el.style.setProperty('--level', smooth.toFixed(3)). The loop runs forever, even when idle.
Consumers:
- CSS: .orb-sm transform scale(1 + level*0.08); .wave i height = 3px + level*11px*k, with k = .5/.85/1/.7/.4 per bar.
- experience.js reads --level from '.hero-orb [data-orb]' (hero sphere: level = --level + emit², rotation += level*0.6) and from the '.dock .orb-sm' mini orb.
dom_contract: [data-orb] (span.orb-anchor in button.hero-orb; span.orb.orb-sm in .dock-orb): inline style --level written
features.config_and_data: Gain 2.2, clamped to 1, smoothing 0.35 per frame.
features.port_notes: Naming collision: in the new project, [data-orb] is the orb scene root and carries a value (data-orb='champagne|porcelain|pearl'); boot.ts finds it with querySelector('[data-orb]'). In the old site, a bare [data-orb] means 'write --level here'. Give level hosts a new hook (e.g. data-level). Feed the new stage with window.amariyaOrb.setAmpSource(() => smoothedLevel), and extend stage.ts so the level also applies while listening (mic input); today stage.ts zeroes it unless speaking. Stop the loop when there is no conversation (it writes three style properties every frame forever) and when the Pause motion control is on. Optionally pass getOutputByteFrequencyData() to the shaders for per-band movement.

features.name: 13. Join chime
features.what_it_does: Plays a soft two-note chime when she joins the call.
features.how_it_works: chime() creates a new AudioContext and plays sine notes at 660 Hz (t = 0) and 880 Hz (t = 0.12 s). Each note's gain rises from 0 to 0.06 in 20 ms, falls exponentially to 0.0001 by +0.35 s, and stops at +0.4 s. The context closes after 800 ms. Everything is in try/catch, and onConnect calls it.
features.config_and_data: Hard-coded frequencies and gains.
features.port_notes: Create or resume the AudioContext inside the click handler. onConnect runs later, outside the user's gesture, so iOS Safari can leave the context suspended and silent. If a sound toggle is added (as on Explore Primland), the chime must respect it. Each niche could have its own two notes (e.g. a hotel bell, a softer clinical tone).

features.name: 14. Ending a session
features.what_it_does: Ends the call from any talk control or the end button, or when the agent ends it (end_call tool), then resets the UI with a friendly caption.
features.how_it_works: stop(): c = conversation; conversation = null; stopUi(); await c?.endSession() in try/catch. onDisconnect also calls stopUi(). stopUi(): conversation = null; muted = false; #muteBtn aria-pressed = 'false'; remove the typing dots; openPanel(false); setState('idle'); then the caption: 'Thanks for chatting — tap the orb to pick it back up.' if the thread has messages, otherwise 'Press the orb and say hello.' The transcript stays in #thread until the next start clears it.
features.config_and_data: The agent has the end_call system tool (AGENT_SETUP line 51).
features.port_notes: Use onDisconnect(details).reason to tell apart an ending by the visitor ('user'), by the agent through end_call ('agent'), or by a fault ('error'), e.g. 'Amariya ended the call' versus 'Connection lost'. Reset the mute aria-label. Consider keeping the transcript readable after the call, with a 'continue by text' option.

features.name: 15. Polite agent navigation: goTo, smooth scroll, follow pill, URL hash
features.what_it_does: When the agent moves the page, it scrolls smoothly. If the visitor is reading or scrolling at that moment, a pill appears instead ('Amariya is showing {section}') rather than pulling the page away.
features.how_it_works: Input tracking: passive window listeners for wheel, touchmove, keydown and pointerdown. Events inside #dock, .sheet or .follow-pill are ignored; any other sets lastUserInput = now and cancels a running agent scroll. goTo(section, fromAgent): el = document.getElementById(section) (any id works); returns false if none. - From the agent: lastAgentScroll = now. If the visitor's last input was under 2500 ms ago and section differs from currentSection: pillTarget = section; the pill's = SECTION_LABELS[section] || section; show the pill; return true without scrolling. - Otherwise: hide the pill, smoothScrollTo(el), history.replaceState(null, '', '#' + section), return true. Pill click: hide it, lastAgentScroll = now, smoothScrollTo(pillTarget). The hash is not updated. smoothScrollTo(el): cancels any previous scroll; target = el's top + scrollY - (.topbar height || 0) - 12. No .topbar exists, so the offset is 12px. Under reduced motion it jumps instantly. Otherwise duration = min(1100, max(500, |distance|*0.45)) ms with easeInOutCubic (t < .5 ? 4t³ : 1 - (-2t+2)³/2), driven by requestAnimationFrame and scrollTo({behavior: 'instant'}), and it can be cancelled. SECTION_LABELS = {welcome: 'the intro', profile: PAGE.sectionLabel || 'your hotel', features: 'features', pricing: 'plans', demo: 'demo booking'}. Pill markup: button#followPill.follow-pill[hidden], text '{brand} is showing ' plus a down-arrow icon.
dom_contract: document.getElementById(<section>) for any section name the agent sends
.topbar: read for an offset but absent (dead)
features.config_and_data: Visitor-input grace period 2500 ms; agent-scroll attribution window 1800 ms (see feature 16); labels from PAGE.sectionLabel.
features.port_notes: Today Lenis (desktop only, in experience.js) and this requestAnimationFrame + window.scrollTo loop both move the page. In the port, send agent navigation through the concept's own scroll engine: lenis.scrollTo(target, {offset, duration, easing}) when Lenis runs, native scrolling otherwise, cancelled on visitor input. For concepts that don't scroll vertically (chapters, horizontal rooms, a chart metaphor), goTo must call the concept's own navigation (open chapter N, turn to a room). Give each concept a navigator that accepts the same five section names. Keep the 'don't pull the page while they read' rule with its follow prompt, keep the hash update, and keep excluding the dock, sheet and pill from reading detection.

features.name: 16. Section tracking and 'visitor moved on their own' reports
features.what_it_does: Tracks which of the five guided sections is on screen and tells the agent when the visitor got there by themselves.
features.how_it_works:
An IntersectionObserver watches #welcome, #profile, #features, #pricing and #demo with rootMargin '-45% 0px -50% 0px', a thin band 45-50% down the viewport. When one intersects:
- currentSection = id.
- The follow pill hides if it points to that id.
- .active, .done and aria-current are toggled on .step elements. This is dead code: no .step exists.
- If more than 1800 ms have passed since the agent's last scroll: contextUpdate('The visitor scrolled to the "{id}" section of the website on their own.').
#story and #faq are not tracked.
dom_contract: #welcome, #profile, #features, #pricing, #demo: all must exist; observer.observe(null) throws and stops everything after line 220 of app.js
#welcome also has class 'section hero' (scroll reveal skips it)
features.config_and_data: SECTIONS = ['welcome', 'profile', 'features', 'pricing', 'demo']
features.port_notes: These five names are part of the agent's API: the navigate_to_section enum and the prompt's 'Website steps'. Keep them as element ids, or as a per-concept map from name to element, and guard missing targets. Consider reporting the new interactions as context updates too (founders' ledger, FAQ, story chapters, sound and day/night toggles). The prompt already tells her to acknowledge such updates naturally without reading them out.

features.name: 17. Scroll reveal (owned by app.js)
features.what_it_does: Section headings and cards rise out of a slight blur as they come into view.
features.how_it_works: An IntersectionObserver with rootMargin '0px 0px -8% 0px' targets '.section:not(.hero) .section-head' and '.section:not(.hero) .card'. Card siblings after the first get --d = min(index, 5) * 0.07s. Each target gets .reveal, then .in once visible, and is unobserved. CSS: .reveal is opacity 0, translateY(28px), blur(8px), with .9s transitions; .reveal.in is fully visible. Under reduced motion, .reveal is always visible.

features.name: 18. In-page nav links [data-nav]
features.what_it_does: Links that take the visitor to a guided section with the same smooth scroll.
features.how_it_works: A click on any [data-nav] calls preventDefault, then goTo(a.dataset.nav). It is not agent-driven, so the section tracker reports it as the visitor's own navigation. The template has one: the hero note '… or just browse'.

features.name: 19. Business profile form and ROI estimate
features.what_it_does: A form the agent fills in as the visitor talks (name, type, units, monthly calls, languages, challenge), next to a live estimate of calls recovered, extra revenue and staff hours, with a note explaining the assumptions. Visitors can type too, and she notices.
features.how_it_works:
Inputs and config: readProfile() = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(#profileForm)); roiConfig() = {...CONFIG.ROI, ...PAGE.roi}.
computeRoi(p):
- calls = Number(p.monthly_calls) || 0. If that is 0 and Number(p.rooms) is set: calls = round(rooms * (callsPerUnit ?? 12)). Still 0: return null.
- recovered = round(calls * (missedCallRate ?? .25)).
- revenue = round(recovered * (bookingConversion ?? .3) * (avgBookingValue ?? 220)).
- hours = round(calls * (minutesPerCall ?? 4) / 60). Hours use all calls, not only recovered ones.
- estimatedCalls = !Number(p.monthly_calls).
renderRoi():
- [data-roi-title] = 'What {BRAND} could recover for {hotel_name} each month' when a name is set, otherwise 'What {BRAND} could recover each month'.
- If there is no estimate it returns, and the previous numbers stay (they never reset to '—').
- countUp() on [data-roi=recovered], [data-roi=revenue] (formatted with fmtMoney) and [data-roi=hours].
- [data-roi-note] = 'Based on {calls} calls/month{ (unitEstimate) when estimated}, {missed%}% currently missed and an average booking of {fmtMoney(avg)}.'
countUp() starts from el.dataset.value, runs 900 ms with ease-out cubic, is instant under reduced motion or when unchanged, and stores data-value. fmtMoney = en-US USD with 0 decimals.
roiSummary(p), the text the agent hears:
- No estimate: 'Not enough data for an ROI estimate yet — ask for the number of {unitsPlural} or monthly calls.'
- Otherwise: k = round(revenue/500)/2; spoken = k >= 1 ? 'about {k} thousand dollars' : 'about {round(revenue/50)*50} dollars'. Returns 'Estimated monthly impact: {recovered} missed calls recovered, {fmtMoney(revenue)} in extra direct bookings (say it as "{spoken} a month"), and {hours} staff hours freed. Use these exact figures; do not recalculate.'
Hand edits: an 'input' event on #profileForm with e.isTrusted re-renders immediately, then after a 1200 ms debounce calls contextUpdate('The visitor edited their {businessNoun} profile by hand: {JSON of profile}. {roiSummary()}'). renderRoi() also runs on load.
Test vectors (exact output of this code):
- hotels, rooms=80: 960 calls (estimated), 240 recovered, $15,840, 64 h, 'about 16 thousand dollars'.
- hotels, calls=1200: 300, $19,800, 80 h, 'about 20 thousand'.
- hotels, rooms=3: 36 calls, 9, $594, 2 h, 'about 600 dollars'.
- aesthetics, practitioners=4 or calls=600: 150, $16,313, 50 h, 'about 16.5 thousand'.
- dental, chairs=5 or calls=900: 225, $13,500, 60 h, 'about 13.5 thousand'.
- home, locations=1: 800 calls, 200, $15,000, 53 h. home, calls=1000: 250, $18,750, 67 h, 'about 19 thousand'.
dom_contract: select[name=hotel_type]: first option value '' ('Select…'); the others are text-only options from profile.type_options
input[name=rooms][type=number][min=1] (label: Rooms / Practitioners / Dental chairs / Locations)
div#roi.card.roi-card: flash target; contains span.orb.roi-orb (decorative particles drawn by experience.js)
b[data-roi=revenue] (inside .roi-hero), b[data-roi=recovered], b[data-roi=hours]: each stores data-value
CSS: .roi-card.flash adds a gradient ring and glow
features.config_and_data:
Per-page roi constants (feature 1), unitsPlural, unitEstimate, businessNoun.
roi.revenue_label: 'extra direct-booking revenue' (hotels), 'extra consultation revenue' (aesthetics), 'extra appointment revenue' (dental), 'extra booking revenue' (home).
Initial roi.note: 'Add rooms or monthly calls to see your numbers.' (wording per unit).
Placeholders: hotels 80 rooms / 1200 calls; aesthetics 4 / 600; dental 5 / 900; home 1 / 1000.
features.port_notes: Field names stay hotel-named on every niche because they are the agent's tool contract (the README says so); only the labels change. Keep the formula and constants exactly so the numbers shown and spoken match, and keep the pre-rounded 'say it as' phrase, which stops the model rounding badly. Make the summary wording niche-specific: 'extra direct bookings' is hotel wording on every page today. Opportunities: relate the estimate to the founders' licence (months to pay back $2,500 / $3,500 / $3,000, computed by the page, never by the model); sliders or steppers instead of number inputs; reset to '—' when the inputs are cleared. Guard every element lookup.

features.name: 20. Agent form filling with visible typing
features.what_it_does: When the agent sets a field, the visitor watches it typed in letter by letter with a highlight, followed by a short flash.
features.how_it_works:
setField(form, name, value): el = form.elements[name]. Returns false if there is no element, or if value is undefined, null or ''.
- SELECT: v = lowercase value. Finds an option whose value === v, text === v, or text includes v. None found: false. Otherwise el.value = opt.value || opt.text; flash(el); returns true.
- Other fields: text = Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : String(value). If el.value === text, returns true; otherwise returns typeInto(el, text), a promise.
typeInto(): adds .filling. Under reduced motion, or for text longer than 60 characters, it sets the value at once; otherwise it clears the field and adds one character every 14-40 ms (14 + random*26). Then it removes .filling and calls flash(el).
flash(el) adds .flash for 1400 ms.
fillForm(form, fields, params) returns {names: the fields that were set, done: Promise.all(...)}. pendingTyping holds the latest typing promise, so get_roi_estimate and submit_demo_request wait until the page has finished typing. Fills done this way fire no 'input' event, so they never trigger the hand-edit report.
dom_contract: .filling: on a field while it is being typed
.flash: on a field for 1400 ms (also on #roi)
CSS: .flash gives a warm border and tinted background; .filling a warm border and 4px ring (styles.css 278-279)
features.config_and_data: Typing speed 14-40 ms per character; instant above 60 characters.
features.port_notes: Keep this: watching her type at human speed is one of the site's signature moments. Give each niche its own highlight. Keep instant fills under reduced motion and for long text. Keep the fuzzy select matching, since the shared agent sends hotel types even on clinic pages. If a concept replaces selects with chips or segmented controls, setField must match against those options.

features.name: 21. Feature spotlight
features.what_it_does: Highlights the feature the agent is talking about.
features.how_it_works: spotlightFeature(key): el = [data-feature=key], or false if missing. Removes .spotlight from every .feature and adds it to el. Keys: 'answering' is the large live-call card, article.card.feature.feature-lg. 'bookings', 'multilingual', 'guest_requests', 'upsells' and 'integrations' are article.card.feature.pill[tabindex=0] inside .orbit-slot. CSS: .card.spotlight lifts the card and adds a gradient ring; on '.orbit-live .pill.spotlight' (and on hover or focus) the pill expands to show its description.
features.config_and_data: Per page: features.pills[{key, icon, title, desc}]; features.card_title and card_desc for 'answering'.
features.port_notes: Keep the six keys (agent contract). Each concept can present features its own way, but every key needs a target that can be visibly highlighted and explained (description revealed), with a keyboard-focus equivalent.

features.name: 22. Plan recommendation
features.what_it_does: The agent marks a plan 'Recommended for you', shows a one-sentence reason, and pre-selects that plan in the demo form.
features.how_it_works: recommendPlan(plan, reason): el = [data-plan=plan], or false if missing. Removes .recommended from every .plan and adds it to el. If a reason is given, [data-plan-reason] becomes 'Why {el's h3 text}: {reason}' and is unhidden; a call without a reason leaves the previous reason showing. Then demoForm.elements.plan.value = plan. The recommend_plan enum (starter/professional/enterprise) is set in the ElevenLabs dashboard. Until it changes, the page must accept these keys and map them (e.g. starter or professional to the founding licence card, enterprise to a groups/multi-location note), or the tool and prompt must change in the same release. recommendPlan throws if the form has no plan field, or if a reason is given and the plan card has no h3; guard both.

features.name: 23. Demo request form (becomes the founders' application)
features.what_it_does: Visitors or the agent fill in name, business, email, phone, preferred time, plan and notes. On submit the request is saved or sent, and a 'You're booked in' confirmation replaces the form.
features.how_it_works:
Fields:
- input[name=name][required], label 'Your name'.
- input[name=hotel_name][required], label demo.business_label (Hotel / Clinic / Practice / Business).
- input[name=email][type=email][required].
- input[name=phone][type=tel].
- input[name=preferred_time], placeholder 'e.g. Thursday afternoon'.
- select[name=plan]: 'Not sure yet' = '', Starter, Professional, Enterprise.
- textarea[name=notes]. Submit button 'Request my demo'.
Validation, missingDemoFields(d): no name gives 'name'; no hotel_name gives PAGE.nameLabel || 'hotel name'; no email gives 'email'; an email failing /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ gives 'a valid email address'.
Visitor submit: the browser's own required/email validation runs first (the form has no novalidate). Then preventDefault; if anything is missing, toast 'Please add your {missing joined with ", "}.' (which reads 'Please add your a valid email address.' for an email like a@b). Otherwise submitDemo(), then contextUpdate('The visitor submitted the demo request form themselves: {JSON}.').
submitDemo():
1. data = {...form fields, hotel_profile: readProfile(), industry: PAGE.industry || 'hotels', submitted_at: ISO string, conversation_id: conversation?.getId?.() ?? null}.
2. Appends data to the localStorage array 'aria_demo_requests' (try/catch) and logs console.info('Demo request:', data).
3. If CONFIG.FORM_WEBHOOK_URL is set: await fetch(url, POST, Content-Type: application/json, JSON body). Errors are only logged; success is shown either way.
4. [data-confirm-text] = "Thanks {name}! We'll email {email} to confirm your demo{ for {preferred_time}}."
5. demoForm.hidden = true; #demoSuccess.hidden = false; goTo('demo', true); #demoSuccess.focus({preventScroll: true}).
There is no reset and no guard against submitting twice. The agent path (submit_demo_request) skips the browser's own validation.
dom_contract: form#demoForm.card.demo-form[hidden after success]: fields name, hotel_name, email, phone, preferred_time, plan (select), notes; button[type=submit]
div#demoSuccess.card.demo-success[hidden][tabindex=-1] > span.success-mark (tick icon), h3 "You're booked in", p[data-confirm-text] ('Our team will be in touch shortly.')
features.config_and_data: CONFIG.FORM_WEBHOOK_URL (empty today); PAGE.industry; PAGE.nameLabel; demo.title, demo.check2, demo.business_label. Checklist: 'A 20-minute live call with our team', demo.check2 ("{brand} set up with your hotel's details"), 'No commitment, no credit card'. Payload: {name, hotel_name, email, phone, preferred_time, plan, notes, hotel_profile: {hotel_name, hotel_type, rooms, monthly_calls, languages, pain_points}, industry, submitted_at, conversation_id}.
features.port_notes: This becomes the founders' 2-step application. Qualified applicants book a 20-minute call on an embedded HubSpot meetings link, and the invoice follows the call. Keep the submission step pluggable: localStorage and console now, a webhook, later the HubSpot Forms API through an Astro server route (never put HubSpot keys in the client). Keep the agent contract (fill_demo_form and submit_demo_request with name, hotel_name, email, phone, preferred_time, plan, notes), or rename the tools and prompt together, and map those fields onto the application's steps. Add what is missing: an error state when sending fails, a guard against duplicate submits, and a timeout on the network call (the agent waits for submit_demo_request's reply). Decide whether to keep storing name, email and phone in the visitor's localStorage. Keep conversation_id (it links the lead to the ElevenLabs transcript) and industry in the payload. Fix the 'Please add your a valid email address' wording.

features.name: 24. Client tools (agent-to-page API) and window.ariaTools
features.what_it_does: Seven tools the agent calls to drive the page, plus one alias. Each returns a sentence the agent hears; every tool is configured with 'Wait for response'.
features.how_it_works:
1. navigate_to_section({section}): goTo(section lowercased, true). Returns 'Now showing the {section} section.' or 'Unknown section. Use one of: welcome, profile, features, pricing, demo.' Any existing element id works, e.g. faq or story.
2. update_hotel_profile(params), alias update_business_profile: goTo('profile', true); fills #profileForm fields hotel_name, hotel_type, rooms, monthly_calls, languages, pain_points; if hotel_name is given it also fills #demoForm's hotel_name; pendingTyping = done.then(renderRoi); adds the activity line 'Updated your {businessNoun} profile' if anything was set. Returns immediately: 'Updated: {names or "nothing"}. {roiSummary({...current profile, ...params})}'.
3. get_roi_estimate() (async): goTo('profile', true); await pendingTyping; flash(#roi); activity 'Calculated your estimate'; returns roiSummary().
4. highlight_feature({feature}): goTo('features', true). Returns 'Highlighting {feature}.' or 'Unknown feature. Use: answering, bookings, multilingual, guest_requests, upsells, integrations.'
5. recommend_plan({plan, reason}): goTo('pricing', true); recommendPlan(plan lowercased, reason); activity 'Recommended the {plan} plan' on success. Returns 'Showing {plan} as the recommended plan.' or 'Unknown plan. Use: starter, professional, enterprise.'
6. fill_demo_form(params): goTo('demo', true); fills #demoForm fields name, hotel_name, email, phone, preferred_time, plan, notes; pendingTyping = done; activity 'Filled in your demo details'. Returns 'Filled: {names or "nothing"}.' plus either ' Still needed: {missing}.' or ' All required fields are complete.' (missing is checked against the current form merged with params).
7. submit_demo_request() (async): await pendingTyping. If fields are missing, returns 'Cannot submit yet. Missing: {missing}.' Otherwise submitDemo(); activity 'Demo request sent'; returns 'Demo request submitted for {name} ({email}).'
window.ariaTools = clientTools (all 8 functions) is a console test hook. The tools work without a live conversation; contextUpdate does nothing then.
dom_contract: Everything listed in features 15, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 (#profileForm, #demoForm, #roi, [data-feature], [data-plan], [data-plan-reason], [data-confirm-text], #demoSuccess, #thread for activity lines, the five section ids)
features.config_and_data:
Dashboard tool definitions (AGENT_SETUP section 4). Names must match exactly.
- navigate_to_section: section (required; welcome/profile/features/pricing/demo).
- update_hotel_profile, all optional: hotel_name; hotel_type (Boutique hotel, City hotel, Resort, Hotel chain / group, B&B / guesthouse, Serviced apartments); rooms (number); monthly_calls (number); languages; pain_points.
- get_roi_estimate: no parameters.
- highlight_feature: feature (required; the six keys).
- recommend_plan: plan (required; starter/professional/enterprise) and reason (a short sentence shown on the page).
- fill_demo_form, all optional: name, hotel_name, email, phone, preferred_time, plan, notes.
- submit_demo_request: no parameters; call only after the visitor confirms the details read back to them, with the email spelled out.
- The end_call system tool.
update_business_profile is optional in the dashboard; the page answers to both names.
features.port_notes: The tool names, parameter names, enums and the meaning of the replies are the hard contract with the live agent. Implement every tool in each concept through a per-concept presenter (navigate, profile, roi, spotlight, recommend, fill, submit). Keep the 'answer at once, let the page catch up' pattern (update_hotel_profile replies before the typing finishes) and the pendingTyping wait. Keep replies fast, because they hold up her next sentence. Keep a console test hook on window (rename to amariyaTools, optionally aliasing ariaTools). New tools for the new concepts (founders' ledger, day/night, channel chips, sound) must be added in the dashboard and on the page together.

2. 'The visitor scrolled to the "{id}" section of the website on their own.' (section tracker, more than 1800 ms after an agent scroll).
3. 'The visitor edited their {businessNoun} profile by hand: {JSON}. {roiSummary}' (1200 ms debounce, trusted input only).
4. 'The visitor submitted the demo request form themselves: {JSON}.'

features.name: 28. Call timer (none for real calls; a decorative one in the live-call card)
features.what_it_does: There is no timer for the visitor's real conversation with Amariya. The only timer is decorative: the 'Live call' card in the features section plays three scripted calls with an mm:ss counter.
features.how_it_works:
In experience.js, CALLS come from the #callScripts JSON, with built-in hotel scripts as a fallback. playCall(call):
- Sets the meta line and restarts the timer for each call (callStart = now).
- For each line: a typing bubble (800 ms for the caller, 1200 ms for the agent); agent replies stream in word by word at 75 ms per word; the line holds for 900 ms + 22 ms per character.

cross_cutting:
ACCESSIBILITY
- Live regions: #thread is aria-live=polite, so new bubbles and activity lines are announced; #toast has role=status. [data-status] and [data-caption] are not live regions. The new constraint needs orb status in a polite live region.
- Dialog and focus: the start sheet is a native <dialog> opened with showModal (focus trap and Esc), with autofocus on 'Start with voice'. Focus moves to the composer when a text session connects, and to #demoSuccess (tabindex=-1) after a submission.
- Control states: #transcriptBtn has aria-expanded and #muteBtn aria-pressed, each with a matching aria-label. Esc collapses the panel.
- Names: feature pills have tabindex=0 and open on :focus. The hero orb is a real <button> named by its visible label ('Tap to talk' / 'Connecting…' / 'Tap to end'). The dock orb has a fixed aria-label 'Start or end conversation'. Decorative orbs and the wave meter are aria-hidden.
- Other: the skip link goes to #profile. Icon buttons are 40px (collapse 32px, send 38px), below the 44px the new site should meet. Transcript bubbles have no dir='auto'.

REDUCED MOTION
- app.js reads prefers-reduced-motion once at load and does not react to changes. Under it, typeInto fills instantly, countUp jumps to the final value and smoothScrollTo jumps.
- CSS shows .reveal content at once and shortens all animations to .01ms.
- The --level loop keeps animating the dock orb's scale and the wave bars. The port should freeze these under reduced motion and when the new Pause motion control is on, while status text keeps updating.

PERFORMANCE
- app.js runs its own requestAnimationFrame loop forever and writes --level on 3 elements every frame, even when idle. Pause it when there is no conversation.
- There are two IntersectionObservers; the input listeners are passive.
- The SDK warm-up runs 800 ms after load. Keep it lazy: the SDK pulls in livekit-client.
- experience.js runs a second animation loop. The port should use one scheduler; stage.ts already pauses off-screen and caps the device pixel ratio.

TEST HOOKS
- window.ariaTools makes every client tool callable from the console without a live call.
- localStorage 'aria_demo_requests' holds every submission, and each one is logged with console.info.
- There are no automated tests.

ERROR HANDLING
- try/catch wraps contextUpdate, localStorage, the webhook fetch, the chime and the volume reads. Failures show as toasts.
- There is no retry, no offline state and no visible error when the webhook fails.

ROBUSTNESS PITFALLS
- app.js looks up its elements at module top level with no null checks. A missing [data-year] (line 31) or any of the five section ids (line 220, observer.observe(null)) throws while the module is evaluating, and everything after that line (voice, tools, forms) silently never runs.
- A missing #profileForm, #demoForm, #endBtn, #transcriptBtn, #collapseBtn, #muteBtn, #typeForm or #followPill throws at its addEventListener line.
- A missing [data-roi-*] or [data-orb-label] throws whenever renderRoi or setState runs.
- A missing .wave stops the level loop.
- Every concept page must satisfy this contract, or the port must guard every lookup.
- Dead code to drop: the .step stepper toggles and the .topbar scroll offset.

SCRIPT ORDER AND COUPLING
- Order today: inline window.PAGE, then config.js (classic script), then app.js and experience.js (modules, deferred).
- experience.js only reads app.js hooks (body[data-state], body[data-tone], and --level on '.hero-orb [data-orb]' and '.dock .orb-sm'). It never writes conversation state.
- Lenis (desktop only, loaded from jsDelivr, version 1.3.26) and app.js's own scroll loop both move the page. The port must give agent navigation one scroll owner.
- The new project already reuses the same names with different meanings: [data-orb] carries the scene name, [data-orb-talk] runs a simulated preview, and window.amariyaOrb accepts only idle, listening and speaking. Reconcile these names when porting.

PRIVACY AND SECURITY
- The agent is public (authentication off) and its ID sits in client code by design; the domain allowlist is what limits access.
- A webhook URL, if one were set, would be public and unauthenticated. HubSpot must go through a server route.
- Demo-request personal data (name, email, phone) stays in the visitor's localStorage.

INTERNATIONALISATION
- The agent detects the caller's language. The scripted calls include Spanish and Arabic, with dir='auto' on their bubbles. The dock transcript does not set dir.

OTHER
- aria-standalone.html is a generated single-file copy of the home page (per README) and adds nothing to port.

features.name: Boot, frame loop and timing model
features.what_it_does: Motion starts only after the first paint. One requestAnimationFrame loop drives everything: Lenis, state easing, scroll effects, the WebGL field, the three mini orbs and the live-call card. Under prefers-reduced-motion nothing loops; still frames are redrawn only when the page scrolls, resizes or the start sheet opens.
features.how_it_works: boot() runs via requestIdleCallback(boot,{timeout:500}), falling back to setTimeout 120 ms. It calls createGL() → startSmoothScroll() → stillFrames() under reduced motion, or requestAnimationFrame(frame) otherwise. frame(now): dt = min(0.05,(now−last)/1000) (the 50 ms clamp prevents jumps after a tab switch); time += dt. Order each frame: lenis.raf(now) → updateStates(dt) → updateScrollFx() → updateProfileGlow() → updateFeatureStage() → updateEclipse() → updateDemoLights() → drawField(time,dt) (only if fieldGL exists) → updateDrift() → drawMini() for each mini → if callVisible: drawDots(time) and updateCallTimer(). Every smoothing step has the form v += (target−v)·min(1,dt·K), which approximates a time constant τ≈1/K. Helpers: clamp(v,0,1); lerp; smooth(a,b,v), which is smoothstep with edges a,b. stillFrames() draws drawField(2,0.016), drawMini(m,2,0), and layoutDots() + drawDots(2) when the call card is visible. It re-runs on resize, on passive scroll, and when a MutationObserver sees #startSheet's [open] change. reducedMotion is read once with matchMedia at load; there is no change listener.

(1) The loop never stops, even when nothing on screen moves, and there is no Pause-motion control. Gate it on visibility, a global Pause, and whether any pinned scene is on screen; the new OrbStage already has setPaused, an IntersectionObserver and visibilitychange handling. (3) Switch to 1−exp(−dt/τ) as stage.ts does; the τ values are listed per feature. (4) Listen for prefers-reduced-motion changes.

features.name: WebGL particle engine (ParticleOrb)
features.what_it_does: A sphere of soft round points: 26,000 when innerWidth ≥ 700, otherwise 11,000. Colour bands by latitude: deep blues across the top, mint and pale gold at the equator, burnt orange at the bottom, with stray colours mixed in. The rim is brighter and the far side dims to 20%. The same points can morph into a mirrored voice waveform across the screen, a tilted ring, or a calm, twinkling field that fills the screen.
features.how_it_works:
Raw WebGL1: getContext('webgl',{alpha:true, antialias:false, premultipliedAlpha:true, powerPreference:'high-performance'}). One program and one STATIC_DRAW interleaved buffer, stride 48 bytes: aPos vec3 (uniform on the unit sphere: y=U(−1,1), a=U(0,2π), position (√(1−y²)·cos a, y, √(1−y²)·sin a)), aColor vec3, aAlt vec4 (wave x U(−1,1), wave band U(0,1), field x U(−1,1), field y U(−1,1)), aMisc vec2 (seed U(0,1), field z U(−1,1)). One gl.drawArrays(POINTS) per frame. Blend is ONE, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA; clear colour 0,0,0,0; no depth test.

Vertex shader. Breathing: n = sin(dot(p,(4.1,3.3,2.7)) + t·.8 + seed·2π)·.5+.5. r = 1 + (n−.5)·.03 + level·(.05 + n·.2) + speak·level·.09·sin(p.y·12 − t·7) + listen·.035·sin(p.y·7 + t·3 + seed·2) + think·.03·sin(t·5 + seed·40); then r *= 1 − connect·.16·(.6 + .4·sin(t·5 + seed·2π)). sphere = rotX(rotY(p·r, uRot), uTilt).
Wave: env = exp(−wx²·2.2); amp = (.1 + .32·env)·(.75 + level·1.8); wy = sin(wx·7 − t·2.3)·amp + sin(wx·19 + t·3.7)·.05·env; wave = (wx·uWaveSpan, wy·(band·2−1), (band−.5)·.4), a filled mirrored waveform.
Ring: ang = atan(p.z,p.x) + t·.06; rr = 1.55 + (seed−.5)·.34 + sin(3ang + t·.5)·.03; ring = rotX((cos ang·rr, (band−.5)·.05, sin ang·rr), 1.2 + uTilt·.4).
Field: (fx·uFieldSpan.x, fy·uFieldSpan.y, fz) + (sin(t·.15 + seed·30), cos(t·.12 + seed·20))·.06.
Morph order: pos = mix(sphere, wave, uWave) → mix(·, ring, uRing) → mix(·, field, uField).
Projection: persp = 1/(1 − z·.22); gl_Position = (uCenter + pos.xy·persp·uScale, 0, 1). There is no camera matrix.
Shading: front = clamp(z·.5+.5); edge = 1−|sphere.z|; shaped = (1−uWave)(1−uField)(1−uRing); rim = mix(1, mix(.55, 1.45, edge²), shaped). vColor = aColor·uBright·(.9 + level·.45)·mix(1, 1.15, edge·shaped). vAlpha = uAlpha·rim·mix(.2, 1, front)·mix(1, .75 + .25·sin(t·2 + seed·50), uField), so points twinkle only in the field. gl_PointSize = max(1.2, uPoint·persp·(1 + level·.35)).

Fragment shader: discard when d > .5; a = vAlpha·smoothstep(.5, .15, d); output premultiplied (vColor·a, a).

Colour (colorFor(y)): t = y + U(−.3,.3). If t > .15: 88% blue, 7% mint, 5% gold. If −.3 < t ≤ .15: 42% mint, 20% gold, 20% blue, 18% orange. If t ≤ −.3: 86% orange, 8% mint, 6% gold. Each colour is multiplied by k = U(.78, 1.10).

resize() runs every frame: dpr = min(devicePixelRatio, 2); the canvas is sized to client size × dpr when it differs, and gl.viewport is set. uPoint = point·dpr. The main field's point = 1.4·clamp(radius/380, .8, 1.15). uScale = (2·radius/canvasW, 2·radius/canvasH); uCenter is the pixel centre converted to NDC.

features.name: Orb reactions: voice states, tone, level, spin, pointer
features.what_it_does: The orb behaves differently in each state. At rest it spins slowly. It swells with the voice level. Speaking sends vertical bands rippling through it. Listening makes it wobble gently. Thinking makes it shimmer and spin faster. Connecting makes it contract and shimmer. Its brightness follows the agent's emotional tone, and it tilts slightly toward the cursor.
features.how_it_works:
updateStates(dt): s = body.dataset.state || 'idle'; k = min(1, dt·4) (τ≈250 ms); each of connecting, listening, thinking and speaking eases toward 1 when it matches s, else 0. Tone: while speaking, the brightness target is {bright 1.15, soft .85, calm .95}[body.dataset.tone], or 1 for warm/unknown. It eases with the same k and returns to 1 otherwise.
Level = parseFloat(--level on '.hero-orb [data-orb]') + emit²·.45 (the greeting pulse). app.js writes --level every frame: smooth += (min(1, vol·2.2) − smooth)·.35 per frame, where vol = conversation.getOutputVolume() when speaking, getInputVolume() when listening and not muted, else 0.
Spin: rot += dt·(.09 + level·.6 + thinking·.5 + connecting·.8) rad/s, so idle is about 70 s per revolution.
Pointer: a window pointermove listener stores x = clientX/innerWidth − .5 and y = clientY/innerHeight − .5, eased with k = min(1, dt·2.5) (τ≈400 ms). The draw uses rot + sx·.35 (±.175 rad, about ±10° yaw) and tilt = .28 + sy·.14 (16° base, ±4°).
State sources in app.js: onConnect → thinking; onModeChange → speaking or listening; a user message → thinking; text mode → listening. Tone comes from ElevenLabs v3 tags: excited, playfully or laughs softly → bright; softly, sighs or thoughtful → soft; reassuring → calm; warmly, curious or anything else → warm.

features.name: Letter-resolve ('live transcript') headings and word-scrub paragraphs
features.what_it_does: Headings resolve letter by letter out of a blur, in random order, as they enter. Story lines resolve letter by letter as you scroll. Intro paragraphs light up word by word with the scroll.
features.how_it_works:
splitText(el), run only when motion is allowed: label = the collapsed textContent, placed in a .sr-only span. A span[aria-hidden] receives the original child nodes (so <em> is kept). Every non-space character becomes span.ch with --r = random in [0, .62) (3 decimals); spaces stay as text.
data-split="in": .js [data-split] .ch {opacity 0}; [data-split=in] .ch {filter: blur(6px); transition: opacity 1s var(--ease), filter 1s var(--ease); transition-delay: calc(.15s + var(--r)·1.2s)}; .is-in sets opacity 1 and filter none. The longest delay is about .894 s, so the whole heading takes about 1.9 s. The hero title triggers at fonts.ready + 120 ms (1500 ms fallback); all others use an IntersectionObserver with rootMargin '0px 0px -18% 0px' and unobserve once in.
data-split="scrub" (story lines): .js .beat .ch {opacity: clamp(0, (var(--bp) − var(--r))·6, 1)}.
setLetters(el, text) re-splits new text while keeping each index's --r, and refreshes the parent line's sr-only label.
[data-scrub] paragraphs: words become span.w with spaces between. lit = round(clamp((vh·.92 − top)/(vh·.5))·n), so words light up as the element's top moves from 92% to 42% of the viewport. .w is rgba(243,241,236,.2) and .on is .92, with a .4s var(--ease) colour transition; the DOM is only touched when the lit count changes.
features.config_and_data: Random range .62; delay .15 + r·1.2 s; duration 1 s; blur 6 px; IntersectionObserver −18% bottom; scrub band from 92% to 42% of vh. Scrub copy is in page.html (e.g. 'She fills this in as you talk. You can also type here — she'll notice your changes.').

features.name: Live outlined clock and day/night copy
features.what_it_does: The giant outlined clock and the first story line show the visitor's local time. They update on the minute and follow the device's 12- or 24-hour preference. features.how_it_works:
twelveHour = (new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined,{hour:'numeric'}).resolvedOptions().hourCycle || 'h12').startsWith('h1'), so h11/h12 means 12-hour.
clockNow(): hh = 12-hour ? String(h%12 || 12) : pad2(h); mm = pad2(minutes); line = 12-hour ? `${hh}:${mm} ${h<12 ? 'am' : 'pm'}` : `${hh}:${mm}`; night = h ≥ 21 || h < 6.
tickClock(): the face (the first child of [data-clock]) is rebuilt with face.replaceChildren(hh, span.tick ':', mm). --fit = (4/(hh.length+3)).toFixed(3): 1 for '2:14', .8 for '12:05' (always .8 in 24-hour). The story line updates through setLetters, only when the text differs.
Scheduler: setTimeout to the next minute boundary + 50 ms, re-armed each time; a visibilitychange to visible ticks immediately.
At load only: in daytime, [data-daypart].textContent = data-day (fallback 'Your team stays with the guest in front of them.') and the 'night' in #story's aria-label becomes 'day'.
CSS: .beat-time font: 400 calc(clamp(10rem, 36vw, 32rem)·var(--fit,1))/.8 Ranade (512px at 1440 wide); letter-spacing −.05em; color transparent; −webkit-text-stroke 1px rgba(255,255,255,.15); transform translateY(−12svh) scale(var(--ts)), which centres it at 38% to match the orb; opacity calc(var(--to)·.8). .tick: animation 2s steps(1,end) infinite, at 50% opacity .2.

active = beatVis[1] > .55. When the beat is inactive, the next release is due within .3 s of it returning.

R = max(60, view.radius). out = 1 − (1 − clamp(t/.5))³; reach = R·(.06 + .94·out + .16·clamp((t−.5)/.5)); x = clamp(sx·reach, −vw/2 + half, vw/2 − half) with half = w/2 + 16; y = sy·reach; blur = (1 − smooth(0,.35,t))·10 + smooth(.72,1,t)·4 px (none below .3); opacity = smooth(0,.3,t)·(1 − smooth(.64,1,t)); transform translate(−50%,−50%) translate3d(x,y,0) scale(.5 + .5·out).
Pulse: emit decays at 1.6/s and level += emit²·.45.
CSS: .js .greetings is absolute at inset 0. Each li is absolute at left 50%, top 38%, nowrap, H2 size, Ranade, #fff; odd children use 70% white; will-change transform, opacity, filter.

features.name: Live call card (24/7 answering)
features.what_it_does: A wide card that plays three short calls in turn. It shows a 'Live call' chip with a blinking mint dot, the caller line (e.g. 'Room 214 · 11:48 pm') and a running mm:ss timer. Each line appears after a typing indicator, and the agent's replies stream in word by word. Every line sends a ripple through a coloured dot grid from the speaker's side. A 'done' chip with a tick closes each call (e.g. 'Cabana booked for 9 pm'), then the thread fades and the next call starts. It includes Spanish and Arabic (RTL) calls.
features.how_it_works:
CALLS = JSON.parse(#callScripts), falling back to the hotel scripts. runCalls() loops forever. whenVisible() polls every 250 ms until callVisible (IntersectionObserver at threshold .2 on .call-demo) is true and the tab is not hidden.
playCall(): remove .out, empty the thread, set meta, reset callStart. For each [who, text]: show a typing bubble (.mini-bubble.<who>.typing.enter with three <i>); wait 1200 ms for 'a' (agent) or 800 ms for 'g' (guest); replace it with the bubble (dir=auto); fire a ripple. Agent text is split into span.w, revealing one word every 75 ms. Then wait 900 + 22·length ms.
After the last line: add .call-done.enter (svg use #i-tick + span dir=auto), ripple from its centre, wait 3000 ms, add .out to the thread (children fade and move up 10px over .5s), wait 650 ms.
The timer shows mm:ss since callStart and updates in the frame loop while visible.
Dot field (canvas 2D, DPR ≤ 2): a 22px grid with ±2.5px jitter; colour colorFor(1 − 2y/h), blue at the top to orange at the bottom; alpha .16–.42; random phase. Each frame: twinkle .7 + .3·sin(1.3t + phase). Each ripple {x, y, t0}: band = exp(−(dist − 280·age)²/1100)·(1 − age/2.6); dots move 6·band px outward; alpha += .85·glow and size = 1.6 + 1.8·glow px. Ripples expire after 2.6 s. Origins: guest = bubble left + 24px; agent = right − 24px; done = centre. The grid rebuilds when the card becomes visible or on resize, only if the size or DPR changed.
CSS: .feature-lg is a 7fr/5fr grid (one column at ≤960px); .call-demo background #08080a, isolation, overflow hidden; thread is a flex column, gap 10px, height 262px (300px at ≤600px). .mini-bubble: max-width 70%, padding 10px 14px, radius 16. Guest (.g): left, rgba(255,255,255,.08) with a 1px .12 border, bottom-left radius 5, transform-origin bottom left. Agent (.a): right, light fill, ink text, bottom-right radius 5. bubbleIn .55s (from opacity 0, translateY 12px, scale .94). Typing dots bounce over 1.2s with .15/.3 s delays; words fade in .25s; the live dot blinks every 1.6s. Under reduced motion, runCalls never starts: the build's static first call stays and the dots are drawn once.

features.name: Assessment: what felt good vs. what was weak (screenshots, code, commit history)
features.how_it_works:
What was weak:
(1) 3D and interaction. The pointer moves the orb only ±10° yaw and ±4° pitch, with no drag, inertia, touch or keyboard. There is no lighting, depth of field, bloom or refraction: it's a flat point cloud under a fake .22 perspective.
(2) Morphs. They are linear per point, so in transit the orb is a squashed disc (02-y1640). The waveform is fully formed for only about 5% of the story (p .15–.20).
(3) The outlined clock is about 12% white, and the orb covers its middle digits (01-y820).
(4) Particles behind content read as noise: the field behind the plans and FAQ; the orb hidden behind the ROI card (06-y4920); the demo field at alpha .14 is invisible.
(5) Dead air: the marquee band with an empty field above it (05-y4100), the gap after the call card (10-y8200), the empty top of the FAQ (13-y10660).
(6) Stock SaaS rhythm: centred section heads, form plus stat card, three equal plan cards, a frosted form on gradient blobs, a FAQ accordion, and glass pills that the user called 'AI-generated'.
(7) One template recoloured per niche: the same story and the same tags, only the copy changes.
(8) Engineering: four WebGL contexts, layout thrash every frame, a loop that never pauses, no Pause control, no live region for the status, Lenis loaded from a CDN, uRing dead code, and stale header comments (the 'outlined numerals' and the 'orbit ring' were both removed in 8b3de85 and b194925).

cross_cutting:
ACCESSIBILITY
Patterns to keep:
- Split text keeps a .sr-only full label beside aria-hidden letters, and setLetters refreshes that label when the clock changes.
- Every decorative layer is aria-hidden: .fx, beat-time, greetings, story-count, profile-glow, eclipse, demo-backdrop, the call visual, the marquee track, the wordmark and the icons.
- The orb is a real <button>; its visible label follows the state ('Tap to talk' / 'Connecting…' / 'Tap to end') and focus shows a dashed ring offset 10px. Global :focus-visible is 2px white offset 3px; inputs use a border and a 4px ring instead.
- Tags are tabindex=0 and open on focus. The FAQ uses native details/summary. The start sheet is a <dialog> with the voice button autofocused. The skip link goes to #profile.
- aria-current marks the niche switcher, aria-pressed the mute button and aria-expanded the transcript button. #thread is aria-live=polite and #toast is role=status. Bubbles use dir=auto for Arabic.
Gaps to close in the port:
- No live region for the orb or dock status; the new Orb.astro has p.sr-only[role=status][data-orb-status].
- No Pause-motion control (needed for the marquee, blob drift, ring spin, colon blink, greetings, call playback and orb idle motion).
- Text that fails AA on rendered pixels: unlit scrub words at 20% white, story-count at 60%, the 50% 'faint' captions and the hero note. The clock and wordmark strokes are decorative and aria-hidden.
- The orb button's accessible name lacks the brand.
- reducedMotion is read once with no change listener.

REDUCED MOTION
In JS:
- No letter or word splitting and no Lenis.
- No loop: still frames are redrawn on scroll, resize and when the sheet opens. The particle view snaps to each scene's target.
- The story never computes progress (beats render stacked) and no greetings play.
- The features stage stays a grid (no .orbit-live).
- The call card never plays; the static first call stays and the dots are drawn once.
- The profile glow, eclipse, demo parallax, risers, glows and wordmark drift don't update. The planet's CSS defaults (--rise 0, --glow 1) show it fully risen.
In CSS:
- html scroll-behavior is auto, .reveal shows instantly, and all animations run .01ms once. The marquee is off.
- Story beats stack statically; the clock, greetings and counter are hidden.
- CSS transitions (rim light .9s, tag open .5s, hovers) still run.

PERFORMANCE PATTERNS
Kept:
- Boot deferred with requestIdleCallback (timeout 500, fallback setTimeout 120). DPR capped at 2. Point counts by width (26k / 11k at 700px).
- One static interleaved buffer and one drawArrays per orb; every morph happens in the vertex shader via uniforms, with no per-frame uploads.
- DOM effects are skipped off screen (±80 to 200px margins).
- The call card is gated by an IntersectionObserver at .2, and its async script polls every 250 ms while hidden. The dot canvas rebuilds only on size or DPR change. Scrub words are rewritten only when the lit count changes.
- will-change on greetings, fh-a, orbit slots, the profile blob and the blobs; every move uses translate3d.
To avoid in the port:
- Four WebGL contexts.
- resize() every frame (clientWidth reads and gl.viewport).
- About 30 layout reads interleaved with style writes every frame.
- A loop that never pauses.
- Animated filter: blur on greetings and fh-a.
- Many large backdrop-filters: the 26px half globe over 1100px, five moving tags at 18px, the dock at 20px, the demo form at 20px, plan cards at 10px, the switcher at 14px.
- Two 80px-blurred blobs.
- Lenis imported from a CDN at runtime.
The new stage.ts already provides DPR caps (1.5, or 1.25 on coarse pointers), offscreen and hidden-tab pausing, context-loss handling and a one-time slow-device degrade (frames over 20 ms after a 1.5 s warm-up).

TEST HOOKS
- Data attributes: data-orb, data-orb-label, data-split=in|scrub, data-scrub, data-clock, data-clock-line, data-daypart, data-day, data-beat, data-count, data-feature (bookings|multilingual|guest_requests|upsells|integrations|answering), data-plan (starter|professional|enterprise), data-plan-reason, data-call-thread, data-call-meta, data-call-timer, data-roi (revenue|recovered|hours), data-roi-title, data-roi-note, data-status, data-caption, data-live-only, data-nav, data-year, data-confirm-text, data-lenis-prevent.
- State attributes: body[data-state][data-tone] and #dock[data-state][data-mode][data-tone].
- Classes: html.js, html.no-webgl, html.lenis, #features.orbit-live, .is-in, .w.on, .spotlight, .recommended, .flash, .filling, .reveal/.in, .expanded, .call-thread.out.
- Data islands: script#callScripts (JSON), window.PAGE (industry, labels, ROI assumptions, greetings, agentContext), window.SITE_CONFIG (BRAND, AGENT_ID, FORM_WEBHOOK_URL, ROI).
- Earlier manual QA, from commit messages: greeting overlap sampled every 150 ms for 12 s on desktop and phone; 12 viewport sizes from 360 to 2560 wide; the features ring checked from 1024×768 to 1920×1080, including 1536×760.

ERROR HANDLING
- createGL wraps the main ParticleOrb in try/catch (shader compile and link errors are thrown): on failure, html.no-webgl, a console.warn, and no minis. Each mini has its own try/catch and its canvas is removed on failure.
- A failed Lenis import → console.warn and native scroll.
- The #callScripts JSON parse is in try/catch, falling back to the hotel scripts.
- document.fonts.ready has a 1500 ms fallback timer; requestIdleCallback falls back to setTimeout.
- Optional elements are guarded with ?. and early returns.
- app.js: a mic NotAllowedError switches to text with a toast; other start errors toast 'Couldn't start the conversation. Please try again.'
- Not handled in the old build: WebGL context loss (stage.ts handles webglcontextlost) and the day/night copy after load.

features.name: Build pipeline and template mechanics (tools/build_pages.py + src/page.html)
features.what_it_does: Renders one HTML template (src/page.html), one JSON content file per page (industries/<key>.json) and a shared registry (industries/site.json) into four static pages: index.html (home), hotels/index.html, aesthetics/index.html and dental/index.html. It also writes sitemap.xml and robots.txt. Nothing is templated at runtime; per-page behaviour reaches the browser through two inline JSON payloads (window.PAGE and script#callScripts). tools/build_standalone.py inlines styles.css, config.js, app.js and experience.js into index.html to make aria-standalone.html (home page only).
features.how_it_works: Placeholders are {{key}} or {{key|attr}}, where key is word characters and dots. Lookup checks the computed values first, then walks a dotted path into the page JSON (e.g. story.beat2_day); a missing key aborts the build with “<page>.json is missing '<key>'”. |attr HTML-escapes the value, quotes included. Without |attr the value is inserted RAW, so content JSON is trusted HTML (<em>, <a href>, pre-escaped &). Before rendering, fill_tokens() recursively replaces {brand} (“Amariya”), {company} (“Amariya AI”) and {base} ('' on home and with --flat, '../' on sub-pages) in every JSON string. {part} is deliberately left alone; app.js fills it at runtime. After rendering, any leftover {{ or {brand|base|company} aborts with “Unfilled placeholder left in <page>”. Computed values: brand, company, version (asset cache-bust ?v=12), base, home (base or './'), url (site_url + page.path), site_url, jsonld, and the generated blocks type_options, marquee_row, pills, call_meta, call_thread, plans, faq_items, industry_nav, page_json and call_scripts (exact markup is in each section's entry). PLAN_NAMES = {starter: Starter, professional: Professional, enterprise: Enterprise}. Plans follow JSON dict order (starter, professional, enterprise). A price starting with '$' gets <small>/month</small> and a JSON-LD Offer; anything else (e.g. 'Custom') renders as-is. Inline JSON uses json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) with every '<' replaced by the escape <. JSON-LD uses indent=2, replaces '</' with '<\/' and indents every line by two spaces. CLI flags: --only <key>, --flat, --brand, --site-url, --out <file>; with --only or --out the sitemap/robots step is skipped. Output is UTF-8 with LF line endings. sitemap.xml lists every site.pages entry, home included, with lastmod = build date. robots.txt has its first '# ' line rewritten to “# {brand} — AI receptionist for hotels and clinics” and its Sitemap: line to {site_url}sitemap.xml.

features.name: Story: a night (or day) at the front desk (#story)
features.what_it_does: A pinned, scroll-driven story in three beats, told at the visitor's own local time. (1) A giant outlined live clock and the line '{time}. A guest calls about a late check-in.' (2) Greetings in nine languages fly out of the orb while 'Amariya answers on the first ring, in their language.' (3) 'The booking lands in your PMS. Your night team sleeps.' By day the last clause becomes 'Your team stays with the guest in front of them.' A counter reads 01 / 03 with a progress bar.
features.how_it_works: Clock: 12- or 24-hour, from the Intl.DateTimeFormat hourCycle. The big clock is hh + span.tick ':' (blinking) + mm, and --fit scales 3-digit against 4-digit times. The line reads 'h:mm am/pm' or 'HH:mm' and swaps letter by letter, keeping its .ch spans and updating the sr-only copy. It updates on the minute (+50 ms) and on visibilitychange. Night is 21:00–05:59. By day, [data-daypart] text becomes data-day (fallback 'Your team stays with the guest in front of them.') and the #story aria-label has its first 'night' replaced with 'day'. Scroll progress p = -top / (height - viewport height). Beat windows are [0, .28], [.28, .68] and [.68, 1.01] with smoothstep fades, written as --vis and --bp per beat. The beat-time gets --to (fades out over .2–.3) and --ts (scale 1.14 → 1). The counter shows 01/02/03, its bar follows --sp, and it fades after .95. Greetings: while beat 2's visibility is above .55, one greeting is released every 1.05 s, alternating four slots ([1.75,-.3], [-1.25,-1.1], [1.25,-1.1], [-1.75,-.3] in orb radii). Each lives 2.1 s (emerges from the centre, un-blurs, drifts out, fades), stays inside the viewport and pulses the orb. The particles morph sphere → mirrored voice waveform (p .06–.28) → full-screen field of points (.68–.82). Beat lines are h2[data-split=scrub], letters split and driven by CSS through --bp.
