features.name: ROI estimate card (#roi)
features.what_it_does: A live estimate beside the profile. Eyebrow 'Your estimate'; title 'What Amariya could recover each month', which becomes 'What Amariya could recover for {name} each month' once a name is entered. A large revenue figure with a per-niche label (e.g. 'extra direct-booking revenue'), then 'calls recovered' and 'staff hours freed'. The note first reads 'Add rooms or monthly calls to see your numbers.' and later explains the basis. The numbers show as '—' until there is input.
features.how_it_works: config = {...SITE_CONFIG.ROI, ...PAGE.roi}. calls = monthly_calls, or round(units × callsPerUnit) when only units are given; that sets an estimatedCalls flag, and app.js falls back to callsPerUnit 12. recovered = round(calls × missedCallRate). revenue = round(recovered × bookingConversion × avgBookingValue). hours = round(calls × minutesPerCall / 60). Figures count up over 900 ms (ease-out cubic; instant under reduced motion) and use en-US formats, revenue in whole USD. Note: 'Based on {calls} calls/month ({unitEstimate}), {missedCallRate × 100}% currently missed and an average booking of {avgBookingValue}.'; the bracket only appears when calls were estimated. The agent gets roiSummary: 'Estimated monthly impact: {recovered} missed calls recovered, {revenue} in extra direct bookings (say it as “about K thousand dollars a month”), and {hours} staff hours freed. Use these exact figures; do not recalculate.' K = round(revenue / 500) / 2, or the nearest $50 below $1k. get_roi_estimate waits for any typing to finish, flashes #roi and logs 'Calculated your estimate'. The page's particle orb anchors on #roi (radius .34 of the shorter screen side, alpha .5), and a still 2,200-point mini orb renders in .roi-orb.

It must also show minutes: the licence includes 500 minutes a month, while the same examples need 3,000–4,800 minutes for all calls, or 750–1,200 for recovered calls alone, at 4–5 minutes per call. features.name: Section 3: Features orbit stage (#features)
features.what_it_does: A pinned scroll transition on desktop (761px and wider, motion allowed). State A: the heading '03 — What she does' / 'Everything your front desk does on the phone' is centred over the sphere, with five slim feature tags spread across the screen. State B: the heading moves to the top-left, the lede appears top-right and the tags settle evenly around the particle sphere, 72° apart with one at the top. Hover, focus or the agent's spotlight opens a tag to show its description. Phones and reduced motion get a plain grid. Below sits the large answering card (next entry).
features.how_it_works: experience.js toggles #features.orbit-live (min-width 761px and motion allowed); the stage is 260vh tall with a sticky 100vh pin. t = clamp((progress - .15) / .5), smoothstepped to e. .fh-a fades, blurs and shrinks out by e × 2.2; .fh-b fades in from e = .5; the lede from e = .55. Pills move from fixed screen fractions [[.14,.15], [.86,.2], [.08,.72], [.93,.66], [.27,.86]] to ring angles [-90, -18, 198, 54, 126]°. The ring distance is solved by bisection so each pill's nearest edge is R + gap from the sphere's centre, with R = lerp(.3, .21, e) × min(viewport height, .62 × viewport width) and gap ≥ 28px. Pills breathe ±4px and bob individually before settling, and stay 16px from the screen edges and 92px above the dock. Each pill gets --lx/--ly (light direction from the sphere), --tint (blue above to orange below) and --ta. highlight_feature(key) scrolls to #features and adds .spotlight to [data-feature=key], removing it from every other .feature.

features.name: Live call card (data-feature=answering) and call scripts
features.what_it_does: A large card under the stage with a 'Live call' indicator, the caller line (e.g. 'Room 214 · 11:48 pm'), a running timer and a chat-style transcript of a short phone call that plays itself: typing dots, the caller's line, Amariya's reply streaming word by word, then a ticked outcome ('Cabana booked for 9 pm'). Three calls rotate per page, one of them in another language (Spanish or Arabic). A dot field behind ripples from whoever is speaking. Text below the visual: '24/7 call answering' plus card_desc.
features.how_it_works: The static markup is the first call, which doubles as the no-JS and reduced-motion fallback. experience.js parses #callScripts (falling back to hard-coded hotel calls) and loops. Each line shows a typing bubble (800 ms for the caller, 1,200 ms for Amariya), then the bubble; Amariya's replies reveal one word every 75 ms. Each line holds for 900 ms + 22 ms per character. Then .call-done shows a tick and the outcome for 3 s, the thread gets .out for 650 ms, and the next call starts. It runs only while the card is at least 20% visible and the tab is visible. The timer counts mm:ss from each call's start. Canvas: a 22px dot grid coloured by height, twinkling, with ripples at 280 px/s that last 2.6 s, starting from the speaker's side. Bubbles carry dir=auto so Arabic renders right-to-left.

When the visitor submits with fields missing, a toast says 'Please add your {list}.', where the list uses 'name', page.nameLabel, and 'email' or 'a valid email address'. Otherwise submitDemo() builds {...form, hotel_profile: the profile form values, industry: PAGE.industry, submitted_at (ISO), conversation_id or null}, appends it to the localStorage array aria_demo_requests, logs it with console.info, and POSTs the JSON to SITE_CONFIG.FORM_WEBHOOK_URL if one is set. It is currently empty, so nothing is sent anywhere. The form then hides, #demoSuccess appears and takes focus with the text 'Thanks {name}! We'll email {email} to confirm your demo{ for {preferred_time}}.', the page scrolls to #demo, and the agent is told 'The visitor submitted the demo request form themselves: {JSON}.' Agent tools: fill_demo_form types the fields and returns 'Filled: … Still needed: …' or '… All required fields are complete.'; submit_demo_request waits for typing to finish, refuses with 'Cannot submit yet. Missing: …', or submits and returns 'Demo request submitted for {name} ({email}).'

features.name: Conversation dock, transcript panel and composer (#dock)
features.what_it_does: A persistent bottom dock with a small voice-reactive orb button; a status line ('Amariya is ready to talk', 'Connecting', 'Listening', 'Thinking', 'Amariya is speaking', 'Mic muted', 'Your turn'), shown uppercase via CSS; a 5-bar wave; a live caption ('Press the orb and say hello.'); and, while live, transcript, mute and end buttons. The panel shows the conversation thread with activity lines and a typing composer.
features.how_it_works: setState(state) writes dock[data-state], dock[data-mode] (voice or text) and body[data-state]; sets the status text from STATUS and the hero orb label; hides [data-live-only] when idle or connecting; and hides #muteBtn in text mode. Captions swap with a 120 ms .swap fade, and user lines are prefixed 'You: '. Tone tags in the agent's text ([excited] etc.) set data-tone to bright, soft, calm or warm on the dock and body (tinting the orb) and are stripped from display. The thread uses li.msg.user, .ai, .activity or .typing (three i elements with aria-label '{brand} is thinking'). Composer submit calls sendUserMessage; typing calls sendUserActivity. Escape closes the panel unless the sheet is open. Audio level: getOutputVolume while speaking, getInputVolume while listening and not muted, smoothed (gain 2.2, k .35) into --level on every [data-orb] and .wave. A 1,400-point WebGL mini orb in .dock .orb-sm reacts to the voice. After a call the caption reads 'Thanks for chatting — tap the orb to pick it back up.' (or 'Press the orb and say hello.' if nothing was said).
dom_contract: aside.dock#dock[data-state=idle|connecting|listening|thinking|speaking][data-mode=voice|text][data-tone][aria-label='Conversation with {{brand}}'] (.expanded when the panel is open)

features.port_notes: Keep in every concept, styled to fit it: one always-reachable talk/text control, a status screen readers hear, captions, the transcript, mute, end, Escape to close and the text fallback. The old status span is NOT in a live region (only the thread is), and the new spec requires orb status in one. Mapping to the new orb: window.amariyaOrb.setState supports only idle, listening and speaking, plus setAmpSource(fn). The old site also had connecting and thinking states and tone tints driven by v3 audio tags; add them or map them (connecting and thinking → idle with distinct motion), and feed setAmpSource from getOutputVolume/getInputVolume. The old hero, dock and sheet orbs were three synced orbs; the new design may use one movable orb, but status must stay visible when the hero is off screen.

features.name: Start sheet (#startSheet) and toast (#toast)
features.what_it_does: Before the first mic prompt, a modal sets expectations: 'Say hello to Amariya'. Three points: 'A quick chat, about 3 minutes. She'll ask about your hotel and walk you through the site as you talk.' / 'Uses your microphone. Your browser will ask for permission. You can mute or switch to typing any time.' / 'Interrupt her whenever you like, just like a normal conversation.' Buttons: 'Start with voice' (autofocus), 'Type instead', and close. A toast shows short notices.
features.how_it_works: requestStart('voice'): with no AGENT_ID it shows the toast 'Add your ElevenLabs agent ID in config.js to enable voice.'; text mode starts immediately; once the sheet has been answered (sheetSeen) voice starts directly; otherwise showModal(), and on close with returnValue voice or text it calls start(mode). start() asks for the mic first. NotAllowedError shows 'No microphone access — switching to text chat.' and switches to text. Connection errors show 'Connection hiccup — please try again.' or 'Couldn't start the conversation. Please try again.' A two-note chime (660 Hz → 880 Hz) plays on connect. The toast fills #toast and adds .show for 2.8 s. A 2,400-point voice-reactive mini orb renders in .sheet .orb-xs.

features.how_it_works: Tools (all with 'wait for response'): navigate_to_section({section}) with one of welcome, profile, features, pricing, demo → 'Now showing the {section} section.' or 'Unknown section. Use one of: …'. update_hotel_profile(params) and its alias update_business_profile, with fields hotel_name, hotel_type, rooms, monthly_calls, languages, pain_points → 'Updated: {names}. {roiSummary}'. get_roi_estimate() → roiSummary. highlight_feature({feature}) with answering, bookings, multilingual, guest_requests, upsells or integrations. recommend_plan({plan, reason}) with starter, professional or enterprise. fill_demo_form(params) with name, hotel_name, email, phone, preferred_time, plan, notes. submit_demo_request(). Session: @elevenlabs/client@1.25.0 (jsDelivr ESM, pre-loaded 800 ms after page load). Voice mode uses connectionType webrtc after getUserMedia; text mode uses textOnly. dynamicVariables: time_of_day, visitor_status (new or returning), visitor_device (mobile or desktop). overrides: agent.firstMessage = the picked greeting; tts.speed ≈ 1.04 morning / 1.00 afternoon / 0.95 evening (+0.02 on mobile, ±0.02 random); tts.stability 0.3 ±0.04. On connect it sends sendContextualUpdate(agentContext). Further contextual updates cover self-scrolling ('The visitor scrolled to the '{id}' section of the website on their own.', sent only if more than 1.8 s after an agent scroll), manual profile edits and manual demo submission. Section tracking uses an IntersectionObserver (rootMargin -45% 0 -50% 0) over the five ids.

The transcript ol has aria-live=polite and the toast has role=status. Icon buttons have aria-labels; mute uses aria-pressed and transcript uses aria-expanded, with labels swapping Show/Hide and Mute/Unmute. The sheet is a native dialog with autofocus, the FAQ uses native details/summary, pills have tabindex=0 and open on :focus, the success card takes focus (tabindex -1), call bubbles have dir=auto, and inputs are wrapped in labels with required and type=email. GAPS to close in the port: dock/orb status is not in a live region (the new spec requires it); there is no Pause motion control (the marquee only pauses on hover; the new Hero already has data-orb-pause); the hero orb button relies on its visible 'Tap to talk' text; greeting words have no lang; the entire call transcript is hidden from assistive tech; the forms do nothing without JS; 'Most popular' and 'Recommended for you' show state only visually. ITALICS: every <em> in the content is emphasis shown upright in the accent colour (styles.css 51 and 303 set font-style: normal on h1 em, h2 em and .fh-b-title em). The new global.css only does this for '.hero h1 em', so add a global rule (em, i, cite, address, var, dfn → font-style: normal) and font-synthesis: none, so no story beat, section title, footer line or data-daypart em can render italic. REDUCED MOTION: app.js scrolls instantly, types instantly and skips the count-up. experience.js skips text splitting, word scrubs, risers, glows, story animation, call playback (the static first call stays) and Lenis; WebGL draws still frames only on scroll, resize or sheet open. CSS hides the clock, greetings and counter and stops the marquee. NO-JS: the .js class gates enhancements; the story beats read as plain h2s with a static 2:14; the first call shows as static markup. PERFORMANCE: a single full-page WebGL point field (26,000 points, 11,000 below 700px wide) plus three mini orbs (2,200 / 1,400 / 2,400 points); DPR capped at 2; the mini orbs and the call canvas draw only when visible, and the call also only while the tab is visible; the particle boot waits for requestIdleCallback (timeout 500 ms); the ElevenLabs SDK pre-loads 800 ms after page load; Lenis runs on desktop only (lerp .09); per-frame work skips off-screen elements. TEST HOOKS: window.ariaTools (every client tool callable from the console), localStorage aria_demo_requests and aria_visited, console.info('Demo request:'), and data-state, data-tone and data-mode on body and the dock. ERROR HANDLING: the build aborts on missing JSON keys or unfilled placeholders. app.js throws at load if any required id is missing (it has no guards). A WebGL failure adds html.no-webgl and a CSS orb fallback. A missing agent ID shows a toast; a denied microphone switches to text mode automatically; connection failures show a toast; webhook failures are only logged. Inline JSON escapes '<' and JSON-LD escapes '</'. The transcript uses textContent, so it cannot inject markup, while content JSON is inserted at build time as trusted raw HTML. HONESTY: the old site contains no testimonials, client logos, ratings, awards or usage statistics, and the new concepts must not invent any. Integration names (Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds, Apaleo), 'no OTA commission', '30+ languages' and every price, minute and guarantee term are claims the owner must confirm. FONTS AND SCRIPTS: the new display faces are latin-only, so the Arabic call script, مرحبا and こんにちは need explicit fallback fonts; keep dir=auto and lang on multilingual lines.

area: Previous design: the visual system and every section as built in styles.css and seen in the 15 screenshots. Also the current Astro hero previews (12 images) and an honest critique, used as the porting contract for the three new concepts.

features.name: Visual system: tokens, colour roles, type scale, radii, easing (previous site)
features.what_it_does: One dark 'night' theme for every page. Home, hotels, aesthetics and dental looked identical; only the words changed. The page is near-black #050506 with warm off-white text #f3f1ec. Hierarchy comes only from white alpha: muted 64%, faint 50%, accent-text 70%. Accent-text is used for the <em> half of every headline, e.g. 'A front desk that never misses a call.' with 'never' in grey. Four orb colours are used only as light (particles, rims, gradient borders, separator dots), never as fills: blue #3e7fd8 (top of the orb), mint #86d6c4, gold #edd685 and orange #e8622a (bottom). Warm #f2a77e marks agent states (typing, speaking). There are two faces. Ranade 400 sets every heading and display line: h1/h2/h3, prices, stats, marquee items, wordmark and clock numerals. Supreme sets everything else. Eyebrows are small, uppercase and tracked, e.g. '02 — YOUR HOTEL'.
features.how_it_works: :root tokens: --bg #050506; --surface rgba(12,12,15,.74); --line rgba(255,255,255,.1); --line-strong rgba(255,255,255,.2); --text and --light #f3f1ec; --muted rgba(243,241,236,.64); --faint rgba(243,241,236,.5); --ink #0b0b0d; --accent-text rgba(255,255,255,.7); --orb-ring linear-gradient(170deg, blue, mint 52%, orange); --radius 22px; --ease cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), used by every transition. Type roles (approved Oct 2026): h1 72/1.05/-.012em (hero only); h2 29/1.14/-.01em (section heads, story lines, footer, marquee); h3 18/1.3 (card titles, FAQ questions, plan names, logo); lead 19/1.5; body 16/1.5 (text, buttons, inputs); card 14; small 13/1.5; eyebrow 12 (.14em, weight 500, uppercase, tabular-nums, faint); kicker and label 11 (.08–.12em caps); stat 34/1.1 (prices, ROI); --head-gap 64. At ≤1068px: h1 56/1.07/-.006em, h2 28, head-gap 48. At ≤734px: h1 40/1.1/0, h2 26/1.15, lead 17, stat 30, head-gap 40. Every heading is weight 400. em is font-style normal plus the accent colour, so there are no italics. Radii: 22 cards, 999 pills and buttons, 12 inputs, 14 icon tiles, 16 bubbles with a 5px tail corner, 26 dock and sheet. Fonts load from a Fontshare stylesheet (ranade@1, supreme@1, display=swap) using the preload-as-style onload swap. html has color-scheme dark, antialiasing and scroll-padding-top 24px. [hidden] is display:none!important. An inline script sets the html.js flag before paint.
dom_contract: h1 em, h2 em (accent colour, normal style)
features.config_and_data: There is no per-niche visual data. Palette, faces and layout were shared by every page; industries/<page>.json only swapped words. Fontshare stylesheet: src/page.html 31-34. theme-color #050506 (page.html 9). An earlier direction was superseded: design-system/aria/MASTER.md, 'Editorial Concierge'. It used navy #0e1116 with gold #d6b370, Fraunces with italics and Inter, and an arch with a service bell and level bars instead of an orb. Its rules said 'no glassmorphism, no glows or radial blobs', and its checklist said 'Content not hidden behind the fixed dock'. The night theme dropped all of this.
features.port_notes: Do not port the values. The new project allows only --color-* role tokens, generated and AA-measured by amariya/scripts/palettes.mjs, so the old alpha-white text system (64/50/20%) has no place there. Any new role a concept needs (unlit scrub text, outline stroke, rim light, glass fill, chart ink) goes into the generator, never hand-written. Keep these principles: no italics (emphasis is colour or weight), tabular numerals for times, prices and stats, one ease curve per concept, and the display face reserved for display. Replace the old h1 72 to h2 29 jump, which made headings feel small and templated, with a scale per concept. The blue-mint-gold-orange aurora on black is the old site's most generic trait; drop it from all three concepts. The old MASTER.md bans (no glass, no glows or blobs) match today's brief; its italics do not.

features.name: Primitives: buttons, icon sprite, focus, skip link
features.what_it_does: Buttons are pills only. The primary '.btn-dark' is a light pill (#f3f1ec fill, #0b0b0d ink), as in 'Talk to Amariya' with a mic icon, 'Request my demo →' and 'Start with voice'. On hover it turns pure white with a 6px halo at 6% white. The secondary '.btn-ghost' is an outline pill at 20% white ('Chat by text', 'Type instead'); its border turns light on hover. Every button presses to scale .97. Arrow icons slide 4px right on hover. The dock uses 40px circular icon buttons. Icons are Iconsax Linear with 1.5px strokes, drawn as inline <symbol>s that follow currentColor. Focus is a 2px solid white outline at 3px offset. A 'Skip to content' light pill slides from top -60px to 12px on focus.
features.how_it_works: .btn: inline-flex, gap .55em, min-height 44px, radius 999, 1px border, font 500 16px Supreme, padding .72em 1.3em. Transitions: transform .25s with the shared ease, colours .2s, shadow .3s. .btn-sm: 13px, min-height 38px, padding .5em 1.05em. .btn-lg: padding .9em 1.55em. .btn-block: full width. .btn-ico: 20px with -2px margin. .btn-arrow: translateX(4px) on .btn:hover. svg:has(> use) gets fill none. The sprite has 17 symbols: i-call, i-calendar, i-translate, i-reserve, i-trend, i-link, i-tick, i-down, i-chevron, i-plus, i-mic, i-mic-off, i-message, i-send, i-end, i-arrow, i-close. :focus-visible is 2px #fff at offset 3. The hero orb uses a 1px dashed outline at 50% white, offset 10px. .icon-btn: 40px circle, 12% border, 6% fill, 12% on hover, scale .94 when active. .icon-sm: 32px. .icon-send: 38px and light.
features.config_and_data: Icons are Iconsax Linear (MIT, via iconsax-react). An inline SVG tick-circle data URI is the bullet in plan lists and in the demo checks. Its stroke is #f3f1ec, or #0b0b0d on the recommended plan.
features.port_notes: Every target was at least 44px except the 40px icon buttons, the 32px collapse button and the 38px send button. Raise those to 44 in the new build. The new project already has its own .btn (52px, primary filled with the accent); each concept should get its own button language instead of the shared pill. The 1px dashed 50% focus ring on the hero orb was too faint. New orbs need a strong focus ring measured against the palette, because they now take Tab focus and keyboard control. Keep the skip link and point it at the first content landmark. Iconsax Linear works but is generic; a concept may draw its own glyphs.

features.name: Header: brand mark and industry switcher (scrolls away; no sticky nav)

The glass segmented pill is generic, and the new Astro Nav repeats it identically on all three niches. Each concept needs its own navigation and scroll paradigm, as the brief asks. Decide whether navigation persists. The old site relied on the dock and the agent's navigate_to_section and had no section menu, so finding your own way round the page was weak. Decide whether a cross-niche home page still exists. At 320px the old three-link bar was near overflow; the new labels are shorter.

features.name: Global WebGL particle field (.fx) and its scenes per section
features.what_it_does: One full-screen particle cloud sits behind the whole page and changes shape for each section; it is the page's single object. In the hero it is a 612px sphere of about 26,000 fine points, blue-lit at the top, mint and gold at the equator, orange at the bottom and brighter at the rim, rotating slowly and tilting a little toward the cursor. On scroll it glides from the hero into the story's centre, flattens into a mirrored voice waveform across the screen, re-forms, then dissolves into a twinkling starfield (01–04). In the profile section it re-forms as a half-transparent sphere centred on the ROI card (06). In features it is a full sphere at the centre of the pinned stage and shrinks as the tags gather (07–09). In pricing, demo and FAQ it becomes a quiet starfield at 35%, 14% and 40% opacity (11–13). In the footer the sphere returns at full brightness, centred on the giant wordmark (14). It reacts to the voice: it swells outward with level, ripples in horizontal bands while speaking, undulates while listening, jitters while thinking, contracts in pulses while connecting, and spins faster with level. Each greeting that leaves it in the story makes it pulse.
features.how_it_works: canvas.fx is fixed at inset 0, z0, pointer-events none, aria-hidden; main is z1. ParticleOrb is WebGL1 with 26,000 points (11,000 if innerWidth < 700) in one interleaved buffer (position, colour, wave x and band, field x and y, seed, field z). Blending is ONE / ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA with soft round sprites: minimum 1.2px, size 1.4·clamp(r/380, .8, 1.15)·DPR, DPR capped at 2. The vertex shader blends sphere → wave (uWave) → ring (uRing, defined but never used) → field (uField). Sphere radius: r = 1 ± noise·.015 + level·(.05 + .2n) + speak·level·.09·sin(12y − 7t) + listen·.035·sin(7y + 3t) + think·.03·sin(5t + 40s), multiplied by (1 − connect·.16·pulse). Colour comes from latitude with stray points: 88% blue above y > .15, mixed in the middle, 86% orange below; brightness varies ×.78–1.1. Rim gain runs .55→1.45 edge-on, depth alpha .2→1, perspective 1/(1 − .22z). Rotation increases by dt·(.09 + level·.6 + thinking·.5 + connecting·.8). The pointer adds .35·x to rotation and sets tilt to .28 + .14·y, using screen-normalised coordinates eased at dt·2.5. State weights ease at dt·4 from body[data-state]. While speaking, brightness follows body[data-tone]: bright 1.15, soft .85, calm .95. Level is --level on '.hero-orb [data-orb]' (set by app.js) plus emit²·.45 from greetings. The active scene is whichever section crosses the middle of the viewport. The 'opening' scene runs while the story's bottom is below the middle: the centre moves from the hero button's rectangle to (vw/2, vh·.38), and the radius moves to .24·minSide, over the first 70% of the hero's height. Scenes: #profile anchors on #roi (r .34, alpha .5); #features uses custom stage geometry (alpha 1; in the grid fallback r .34, alpha .45); #pricing is a field (r .32, alpha .35); #demo a field (alpha .14); #faq a field (alpha .4); .footer anchors on .wordmark (r .21, alpha 1). Below 760px the radius is ×1.15 and alpha ×.8. Easing: position dt·5 (dt·12 in the opening scene), shape dt·2.2, alpha min(k, dt·1.6). Between sections it holds the last scene. It boots on requestIdleCallback (timeout 500) or setTimeout 120. If WebGL fails, html.no-webgl is set.
features.config_and_data: Constants in experience.js: PALETTE (RGB sets for blue, mint, gold and orange), the SCENES table, WINDOWS, TONE_BRIGHT, and point counts 26000/11000. Nothing varies per niche.
features.files_and_lines: C:/projects/aria-hotel-website/experience.js 137-326 (shader and class), 328-349 (states, pointer), 351-555 (scenes, drawField), 976-1002 (createGL), 1021-1072 (loop and boot); C:/projects/aria-hotel-website/styles.css 86-88, 508-518; screenshots 00-y0.jpg through 14-y11480.jpg in C:/Users/user/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--projects-aria-hotel-website/e36307e5-8175-4af0-8549-db4a9f079c44/scratchpad/oldsite/
features.port_notes: Keep the idea. One persistent 3D character that changes form in each chapter and is the agent's body is the old site's strongest asset. Give each niche a different character, material and choreography. The old look, fine dusty aurora particles, reads as a stock three.js example and is too dim to light a hero. Keep the behaviour contract: blending between idle, connecting, listening, thinking and speaking; tone tint; level reactivity both while listening (the visitor's input volume) and while speaking (the agent's output volume); boot when idle; DPR cap; detail tiers; pause when offscreen or the tab is hidden; still frames under reduced motion; a WebGL fallback. The new OrbStage is missing some of this and it must be added. It has only idle, listening and speaking, with no connecting or thinking. It applies amp only while speaking (stage.ts 137). It has no tone. It runs one orb per page (boot.ts 19). Pointer response must grow from a ±.35 rad nudge into real 3D manipulation: drag and throw with inertia, touch, and the keyboard. The old main loop never paused (rAF always on, field drawn every frame); the new stage's pausing on IntersectionObserver and visibility is better, so use it for every canvas.

features.name: Hero 'Welcome' (previous site)
features.what_it_does: (00-y0.jpg) A full-viewport black stage. The particle sphere, 68svh (about 612px on a 900px-tall screen), sits centred at 45% height and is itself the main button. The headline 'A front desk that never misses a call.' is set inside the sphere in white Ranade 72px, centred and balanced, with 'never' at 70% white. On load its letters resolve out of a 6px blur in random order, like a live transcript. Under the sphere is an outlined pill label 'Tap to talk'. It changes to 'Connecting…' while connecting and 'Tap to end' when live. Its border turns mint when listening, warm when speaking and white on hover. At the bottom left is the lede (19px, 64% white, max 390px): 'Amariya is the AI receptionist for hotels. She picks up 24/7, books rooms straight into your PMS and speaks your guests' language — warmly, like your best night manager.' Under it sit 'Talk to Amariya' (light pill with mic) and 'Chat by text' (ghost), then a 13px note, 'About 3 minutes · switch to typing any time · or just browse'. 'browse' is underlined and jumps to #profile. At the bottom right, 'Scroll to explore' sits beside a 44px hairline in which a white segment falls every 2.4s. Behind everything are two very soft radial lights, blue at 50%/36% and orange at 50%/60%, drifting with scroll.

At 1101–1447px it moves to bottom 104px so the 540px dock never covers it.
