features.port_notes: Keep: talking from the hero, a typed alternative, the 'browse' escape hatch, a scroll cue, a visible state label on the orb, and the headline entering like a transcript. Fix: five ways to start one action (orb, 'Tap to talk', Talk button, 'Chat by text', dock orb) read as indecision. Each concept gets one voice CTA and one text CTA. The headline sat inside the orb only because the sphere was hollow and dark. With solid glass, porcelain or pearl orbs, the text must sit elsewhere or be refracted by the object on purpose (Noomo style). The old hero had no Founders' offer; the new one needs price, ledger ('30 · issued · held · open'), guarantee and Apply. In the new hotels preview that offer falls below the fold at 1440×900; do not repeat that.

features.name: Text motion system: transcript letters, word scrub, reveals, risers, glow parallax
features.what_it_does: Four layered text behaviours. (1) Transcript letters: headings marked data-split=in resolve letter by letter, in random order, out of a 6px blur (about 1–1.9s) once they enter the lower 82% of the viewport. The hero title does this when its font loads. (2) Scrubbed letters: story lines (data-split=scrub) appear letter by letter, in random order, as you scroll. (3) Word lighting: section ledes (data-scrub) start at 20% white and light up word by word to 92% as the paragraph rises from 92% to 42% of the viewport. (4) Entrances: section heads and cards rise 28px out of an 8px blur (.9s; cards stagger by 70ms). Large blocks (profile grid, call card, plan grid, demo form, FAQ list, footer CTA) also rise from 110px and scale from .94 to 1 with scroll. Section glows move ±60px with scroll, and the footer wordmark ±45px.
features.how_it_works: splitText() wraps each non-space character in span.ch with --r random in 0–.62. It moves the visual copy into an aria-hidden span and appends an .sr-only copy of the text, so screen readers read the sentence once. CSS: .js [data-split] .ch{opacity:0}. [data-split=in] .ch{filter:blur(6px); transition opacity 1s, filter 1s; delay .15s + r·1.2s}. .is-in sets opacity 1 and filter none. The IntersectionObserver uses rootMargin '0px 0px -18% 0px'. The hero waits for document.fonts.ready + 120ms, with a 1.5s failsafe. Story: .beat .ch opacity = clamp((--bp − --r)·6, 0, 1). Word scrub: words become span.w; lit = round(clamp((vh·.92 − top)/(vh·.5))·n); .w is 20%, .on is 92% (transition .4s). Reveal (app.js): .reveal is added to '.section:not(.hero) .section-head' and to .card. Sibling cards get --d = min(i,5)·.07s. The observer uses rootMargin bottom −8%, and .in clears opacity, transform and filter (.9s). Risers: e = 1 − (1 − clamp((vh − top)/(vh·.75)))³; transform translate3d(0,(1−e)·110px,0) scale(.94+.06e). Glows: --gy = (.5 − p)·120px on .hero, .content .section and .footer. Wordmark: --py = (.5 − p)·90px. Reduced motion skips all of it.
features.config_and_data: Constants only: random --r range .62, delays .15 + 1.2r, observer margins −18% and −8%, scrub band 92%→42%.
features.files_and_lines: C:/projects/aria-hotel-website/styles.css 153-160, 600-602; C:/projects/aria-hotel-website/experience.js 85-135, 591-621; C:/projects/aria-hotel-website/app.js 222-236; blank-heading evidence: C:/Users/user/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--projects-aria-hotel-website/e36307e5-8175-4af0-8549-db4a9f079c44/scratchpad/oldsite/10-y8200.jpg (the '04 — PLANS' eyebrow and the lede are visible; the h2 is not)
features.port_notes: Keep the transcript-style letter resolve and the sr-only twin pattern; they suit a voice product and stay accessible. Three problems must not repeat. Headings stay fully invisible until they cross −18%, so fast scrolling and screenshots show sections with no heading. Unlit scrub words at 20% white measure about 1.6:1 on #050506, so real lede text fails AA until it is scrolled. And three entrance effects stacked on one block (riser, reveal, split) make the generic 'everything fades up' rhythm. New rules: one entrance language per concept; text legible at AA in every in-between state, or the animated layer is a decorative duplicate; nothing gated on an IntersectionObserver alone without a timeout.

features.name: Story: a pinned night at the front desk, set at the visitor's own time
features.what_it_does: (01–04) A pinned 'night at the front desk' in three beats, with a counter '01 / 03' and a 120px progress hairline at the bottom left. Beat 1: a giant outline clock of the visitor's local time sits behind the sphere, then fades and settles from scale 1.14 to 1. Example: '1:04' in Ranade about 512px, with a 1px stroke at 15% white, a colon blinking every 2s, and 12- or 24-hour format following the device. The line '1:04 am. A guest calls about a late check-in.' scrubs in near the bottom of the screen (15svh up). The live time is typed into its first words, and the em part is grey. The sphere flattens into a mirrored voice waveform, then re-forms. Beat 2: 'Amariya answers on the first ring, in their language.' Greetings leave the sphere once every 1.05s: Hello, Hola, Bonjour, مرحبا, Ciao, こんにちは, Olá, Hallo, Merhaba. Each travels to the next of four alternating slots (right, upper-left, upper-right, left), unblurs from 10px, grows from .5 to 1, fades, and makes the sphere pulse. Screenshot 03 shows 'Hola' sharp and 'Hello' blurred. Beat 3: the sphere dissolves into a starfield, with 'The booking lands in your PMS. Your night team sleeps.' Between 06:00 and 20:59 the last sentence becomes the niche's daytime line ('Your team stays with the guest in front of them.'), and the section's aria-label changes from 'night' to 'day'.
features.how_it_works: .js .story is 420svh tall (340svh at ≤600px). .story-pin: sticky, top 0, height 100svh, overflow hidden. .beat: absolute inset 0, place-items end center, padding 0 24px 15svh (20svh on phones), opacity var(--vis). Progress p = −top/(height − vh), eased at dt·7; it snaps if it jumps more than .35, e.g. on agent navigation. Windows: [0,.28], [.28,.68], [.68,1.01]. --vis = smooth(a−.08 or a−.03, a+.05)·(1 − smooth(b−.06, b+.01)). --bp = clamp((p−a)/((b−a)·.6)). Clock: font calc(clamp(10rem,36vw,32rem)·--fit)/.8, letter-spacing −.05em, transparent fill, -webkit-text-stroke 1px rgba(255,255,255,.15), translateY(−12svh) scale(--ts), opacity --to·.8. --to = 1 − smooth(.2,.3,p). --ts = 1.14 − .14·smooth(0,.26,p). --fit = 4/(hh.length + 3). .tick keyframes: 50% opacity .2, 2s steps(1,end). The clock updates on each minute (+50ms) and on visibilitychange; setLetters keeps each letter's --r when the time changes. Greetings: each li is absolute at 50%/38%, h2 size, odd items at 70% white, with transform, opacity and filter set per frame. Slots (GREET_SLOTS, in orb radii): [[1.75,−.3],[−1.25,−1.1],[1.25,−1.1],[−1.75,−.3]]. Each greeting lives 2.1s (0.5s once the beat ends), with x clamped inside the viewport. Counter: 11px, weight 500, .12em, tabular, 60% white with the current number in white. Its i is 120×1px at 18% white, and the b inside scales with scaleX(--sp). The counter fades out at p .95–1. Wave blend: smooth(.06,.15,p)·(1 − smooth(.2,.28,p)). Field: smooth(.68,.82,p).
features.config_and_data: Per niche: story.label ('A night at the front desk' / '…clinic's front desk' / '…practice's front desk'); beat0 (hotels '. A guest calls about a late check-in.'; aesthetics '. A client asks about a consultation.'; dental '. A patient calls with a toothache.'); beat1; beat2 ('The booking lands in your PMS.' / 'The consultation lands in your calendar.' / 'The first free slot is booked.'); beat2_night; beat2_day. The greeting list is hard-coded in page.html 103. Night is 21:00–05:59.
features.port_notes: These must survive in every concept, re-staged rather than copied: the visitor's live local time (12/24h, accurate to the minute, with the day/night copy and label swap); the multilingual greeting moment, including RTL Arabic and Japanese; a three-beat narrative scrubbed by scroll, with a progress counter; and the agent's body changing form in each beat. The old execution was weak and must be beaten. It took about 3,800px of scroll for three 29px sentences parked at the bottom edge. Beat 3 is an empty starfield (04). Halfway from sphere to wave, the shape reads as a squashed disc (02). The greetings are plain grey text. Make each beat a dense visual event, shorten the pin, and tie the clock to the niche: a hotel night shift, a clinic's day list, a dental urgent morning.

features.name: 'Built for' marquee
features.what_it_does: (05-y4100.jpg) A full-width band between two hairlines on a 55% black wash. 'BUILT FOR' (11px caps, faint) is centred above a slow, endless ticker of the niche's categories in Ranade 29px: 'Boutique hotels • Resorts • City hotels • B&Bs • Hotel groups • Serviced apartments'. 10px dots filled with the orb gradient separate the items. The band fades out at both edges (14% gradients), and hovering pauses it.
features.how_it_works: .marquee: padding 36px 0 44px, overflow hidden, --line borders top and bottom, background rgba(5,5,6,.55). ::before and ::after are 14% edge fades to --bg. .marquee-track: flex, gap 44px, width max-content, animation marquee 48s linear infinite (translateX(−50%)) over two identical copies of the row. :hover pauses it; reduced motion makes it static. Screen readers get one .sr-only sentence; the label and track are aria-hidden.
dom_contract: .marquee-track[aria-hidden] > span + i (two copies of the row)
features.config_and_data: marquee.sr and marquee.items per niche. Aesthetics: Med spas, Aesthetics clinics, Laser & skin clinics, Cosmetic surgery, Hair transplant clinics, Clinic groups. Dental: General dentists, Cosmetic dentistry, Orthodontists, Pediatric dentists, Dental groups, Specialist practices.
features.port_notes: The content is worth keeping: who each niche serves helps qualification in the application and helps SEO. The ticker itself is filler with no proof value and a stock pattern, so it is obsolete as a component. If a concept needs a 'who it's for' moment, make it do something: picking your property type could personalise the page and the agent. Or replace it with proof: status per market, real customer logos when they exist, or the founding-licence ledger.

features.name: Section rhythm, cards and cursor light
features.what_it_does: Every section after the story uses the same centred block. First a small numbered eyebrow ('02 — Your hotel', '03 — What she does', '04 — Plans', '05 — Book a demo', then an unnumbered 'Questions'). Then a 29px Ranade h2 with its second half in grey ('Tell Amariya about your property'). Then a 19px muted lede that lights up word by word. Content follows in a 1240px column. Cards are dark translucent panels (rgba(12,12,15,.74), 1px hairline at 10%, radius 22, padding 28), and a faint white light follows the cursor inside them on hover.
features.how_it_works: .content: max-width 1240px, padding 0 clamp(16px,4vw,48px). .section: padding 140px 0 24px (96px top at ≤600); consecutive sections add 96px margin. .content .section::before and .footer::before are a 140vw glow layer using var(--glow), moved by --gy. Only .footer sets --glow, so in practice only the footer glows. .section-head: grid, centred, gap lead·1.2 (12px at ≤960), max 1000px, margin-bottom --head-gap, padding-top 56px. h2 max 980px; .muted lede max 60ch. .card: --mx and --my are set on pointermove, only on devices that can hover. ::after is radial-gradient(360px circle at --mx --my, rgba(255,255,255,.06), transparent 45%) fading in over .4s. Border, shadow, transform, background and colour transition over .35s.
features.config_and_data: Section ids are the agent's navigation targets: SECTIONS = welcome, profile, features, pricing, demo. FAQ sits outside the guided steps. SECTION_LABELS for the follow pill: the intro / your hotel (page.sectionLabel) / features / plans / demo booking.
features.port_notes: Discard the rhythm. The same centred eyebrow, half-grey h2 and muted lede on every section is the most 'SaaS template' part of the old page; the numbering also starts at 02 and stops before the FAQ. Keep stable section ids, or remap navigate_to_section's list and SECTION_LABELS together, so the agent can still drive the page. The cursor-following light is a nice touch, but a hover-only reveal adds nothing on touch. If a concept keeps it, make it part of that concept's material.

features.name: Profile and ROI estimate: frosted dome, spreading warm light, form, ROI card, agent typing
features.what_it_does: (06-y4920.jpg) The heading '02 — YOUR HOTEL / Tell Amariya about your property' and the line 'She fills this in as you talk. You can also type here — she'll notice your changes.' sit inside a huge frosted-glass half globe. The dome is about 1100px wide, with a bright warm 1px rim and a highlight along its top, and it fades out by 44% of its height. A warm amber light glows through it. As you scroll the section, that light slides down from the dome's rim to the middle of the section, grows to at least 2.4× and dims to 34%, becoming a soft wash. Below are two cards (1.25fr / 1fr, 20px gap). The left card is a form: Hotel name ('e.g. The Harbour House'); Type of property, a select with Boutique hotel, City hotel, Resort, Hotel chain / group, B&B / guesthouse, Serviced apartments; Rooms ('80') next to Calls per month ('1200'); Guest languages ('English, Spanish, Arabic'); and Biggest front-desk challenge, a textarea ('Missed calls at night, repetitive questions…'). The right card is the estimate. It has a 1px blue→mint→orange gradient border and a 200px particle mini orb peeking from its top-right corner. It reads 'YOUR ESTIMATE' and 'What Amariya could recover each month', which becomes '…for The Harbour House each month' once a name is typed. A revenue stat spans the full width above a hairline ('extra direct-booking revenue'), with two stats below ('calls recovered', 'staff hours freed'); all show '—' until there is data. A note sits at the bottom: 'Add rooms or monthly calls to see your numbers.' becomes 'Based on 960 calls/month (estimated from room count), 25% currently missed and an average booking of $220.' When the agent fills a field, it gets a warm border and a 4px warm ring while characters appear one by one, then flashes warm for 1.4s. Numbers count up over 900ms. When the agent is asked for the estimate, the whole card flashes with the full gradient border and a 60px warm glow. The global sphere re-centres on the estimate card at 50% opacity.
features.how_it_works: The dome is #profile .section-head::before: a min(1100px,130vw) square circle at top 0. Backgrounds: radial(62% 40% at 50% 0, rgba(255,196,150,.3)→.1→0), radial(90% 55% at 50% 12%, rgba(255,232,214,.07)), and linear(180deg, rgba(255,244,234,.14)→.06 at 22%→.02 at 38%→0 at 50%). Border: 1px rgba(255,236,220,.22). Shadows: inset 0 1.5px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.6) and inset 0 30px 70px −34px rgba(255,214,180,.5). backdrop-filter: blur(26px) saturate(1.35). Mask: linear(#000 from 0 to 16%, transparent at 44%). The eyebrow is rgba(255,238,224,.82). The light is .profile-glow, a full-width layer at z −2, clipped to the section, with mask fades of 120px at the top and 220px at the bottom. Inside it, i measures min(600px,118vw)×440 with radial closest-side rgba(255,160,72,.95)→rgba(255,130,52,.58) at 40%→rgba(250,112,44,.18) at 70%→0, blurred 24px. JS: t = clamp((vh·.3 − top)/(height − vh·.7)), smoothstepped; y lerps from head.offsetTop+10 to height·.5; scale goes from 1 to max(2.4, height·1.05/blobH); opacity from 1 to .34. Inputs: 16px, min-height 44, rgba(255,255,255,.04) fill, 1px --line, radius 12, padding .75em .9em. Hover uses --line-strong; focus uses a --light border plus 0 0 0 4px rgba(255,255,255,.06). Placeholders are 35%. Labels: grid, gap 7, 13px, weight 500, muted, margin-bottom 16. .row2 is two columns with gap 14 (one column at ≤600). .filling: --orb-warm border plus 0 0 0 4px rgba(242,167,126,.14). .flash: --orb-warm border plus background rgba(242,167,126,.1), for 1.4s. ROI card: a 1px transparent border, painted with linear(#0b0b0e) padding-box over linear(170deg, rgba(62,127,216,.7), rgba(134,214,196,.3) 50%, rgba(232,98,42,.7)) border-box. Its flash state uses var(--orb-ring) border-box plus 0 0 60px rgba(242,167,126,.18). Stats: two-column grid, gaps 22/18. Each b is 34px Ranade, tabular, white; each span is 13px muted. .roi-hero spans the full row with a hairline below. The note (.tiny, faint) is pushed to the bottom with margin-top auto. Maths: calls = monthly_calls, or rooms·callsPerUnit (12); recovered = calls·.25; revenue = recovered·.3·$220; hours = calls·4/60. Count-up takes 900ms with an ease-out cubic (instant under reduced motion). Agent typing takes 14–40ms per character, and is instant for text over 60 characters or under reduced motion. Manual edits: renderRoi runs at once, and after 1.2s a contextual update tells the agent the profile JSON and an ROI summary already rounded for speech.
features.config_and_data: Per niche: profile.eyebrow, title, name_label, name_placeholder, type_label, type_options, units_label (Rooms / Practitioners / Dental chairs / Locations), units_placeholder, calls_placeholder, languages_label, languages_placeholder, challenge_label, challenge_placeholder; roi.revenue_label and roi.note; page.roi {missedCallRate .25, bookingConversion .3, avgBookingValue 220, minutesPerCall 4, callsPerUnit 12 for hotels}; page.unitEstimate, unitsPlural, businessNoun, nameLabel. Global defaults are in config.js ROI. Field names stay hotel_* on every niche (an old README rule).
features.port_notes: Keep these behaviours exactly: field names hotel_name, hotel_type, rooms, monthly_calls, languages and pain_points (the update_hotel_profile / update_business_profile tool fills them); the ROI formula and per-niche assumptions; the speech-rounded summary returned to the agent; agent typing with .filling then .flash; context updates after manual edits, debounced; the count-up; and the ROI title personalised with the name. Re-imagine the look per concept: a hotel night ledger or folio, a clinical readout chart with the porcelain instrument, a dental day sheet. Consider folding this profile into step 1 of the Founders' application so visitors type once. The quality to beat: the dome with its spreading warm light was one of the best-lit moments. But the form was a plain dark dashboard form, the '—' placeholders looked broken, and the clipped mini orb read as an accident. Placeholders at 35% measure about 3:1, so new placeholders must pass AA or be replaced by persistent labels and examples.

features.name: Features pinned stage: glass tags gathering round the sphere
features.what_it_does: (07–09) A pinned scene, 260svh tall, on screens at least 761px wide. In state A (07), the eyebrow '03 — WHAT SHE DOES' and the h2 'Everything your front desk does on the phone' sit centred over the particle sphere. Five frosted-glass tags, each an icon and a one-line title, float spread to the corners of the screen, bobbing ±6px: Direct bookings, 30+ languages, Guest requests, Smart upsells, PMS & tool integrations. The fifth is not visible in 07; it is clamped to the bottom edge behind the dock. As you scroll, the centred heading lifts 60px, shrinks 12%, blurs 8px and fades. The tags fly in and settle evenly round the sphere, 72° apart with one at the top: Direct bookings at the top, 30+ languages on the right, Smart upsells lower right, PMS & tool integrations lower left, Guest requests on the left. Each sits the same gap from the sphere's edge, and they all breathe ±4px together. The sphere shrinks and drops slightly. Then a corner heading fades in at the top left (three lines), and the lede at the top right: 'Amariya handles the calls, the questions and the bookings, and hands off to your team the moment a human touch matters.' (08). Each tag's glass takes on the sphere's colour on the side facing it: blue from the top half, orange from the bottom. Hover, keyboard focus or the agent's highlight opens a tag into a small card with its description, e.g. 'Checks live availability, quotes rates and books straight into your PMS — no OTA commission.'
features.how_it_works: experience.js adds .orbit-live when motion is allowed and (min-width: 761px) matches. Then .feature-stage is 260svh and .feature-pin is sticky at 100svh. .fh-a is absolutely centred at z2, with transform, opacity and blur set by JS. .fh-b is absolute at left 0, top 11%, h2 size, max 16ch; it is an aria-hidden duplicate of the title. .feature-lede is absolute at right 0, top 12%, max 380px. .orbit is absolute inset 0, and each .orbit-slot is absolute with a translate3d set every frame. Timeline: t = clamp((clamp(−top/(H−vh)) − .15)/.5), e = smoothstep(t). aOut = clamp(2.2e). fh-b fades in from e .5 over .45, rising 16px. The lede fades in from e .55 over .4, rising 24px. m = 1 − (1 − clamp(e/.85))³. Geometry: base = min(vh, .62·vw); R = lerp(.3,.21,e)·base; cy = lerp(.5,.545,e)·H; gap = max(28, .2R). State A positions (PILL_A, fractions of the screen): [[.14,.15],[.86,.2],[.08,.72],[.93,.66],[.27,.86]]. State B angles (PILL_ANGLE): [−90,−18,198,54,126]°. Distance comes from clearDistance(), a 24-step bisection that puts the box's nearest point at R+gap, plus sin(.9t)·4. Bob = sin(.9t + 1.7i)·6·(1−m). x is clamped 16px inside the viewport, and y above the dock (H − h/2 − 92). Placement uses each tag's closed size so an opening tag does not jump. Glass: radial-gradient(90% 150% at --lx --ly, rgb(--tint / --ta), transparent 70%), plus linear(160deg, rgba(255,255,255,.13), .04 at 42%, .02 at 62%, .07), over rgba(18,18,24,.3). backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.6). box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.2), inset 0 0 14px rgba(255,255,255,.03), 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.35). ::after is a masked 1px rim, linear(170deg, .42 → .1 at 30% → .03 at 62% → .15). --tint lerps from rgb(120,160,255) at the top to rgb(255,140,70) at the bottom, by the tag's height relative to the sphere. --ta = .05 + .15m. --lx and --ly point the light at the sphere. A tag in the live stage: padding 9px 16px 9px 13px, radius 20, icon 16px at 55% white (warm on hover or spotlight), h3 16px, nowrap, 92% white. Open (:hover, :focus or .spotlight): radius 16, background rgba(16,16,22,.62), shadow 0 18px 44px .5; the p becomes 240px wide with max-height 8em and fades in over .4s after .15s. Fallback (under 761px, reduced motion or no JS): .orbit is grid repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px,1fr)), gap 12, max 1000px. Tags become 16px-radius glass cards with their descriptions visible, and they lift 3px on hover.
features.config_and_data: features.title, features.lede and features.pills[{key, icon, title, desc}] per niche. Hotels: Direct bookings / 30+ languages / Guest requests / Smart upsells / PMS & tool integrations. Aesthetics: Consultation booking / 30+ languages / Patient questions / Rebooking & packages / Clinic software. Dental: Appointment booking / 30+ languages / Urgent calls / Recalls & rebooking / Practice software. The agent's highlight_feature keys: answering, bookings, multilingual, guest_requests, upsells, integrations.
features.port_notes: Keep: the five feature keys plus 'answering' (the agent's list); per-niche titles and descriptions; descriptions that open on hover, keyboard focus and agent spotlight; keyboard focus on every feature; and, if a concept wants it, a pinned scene where features gather to the agent. Do not port the look. Glass capsules orbiting a glowing sphere (taken from mdx.so) is exactly the 'glassmorphism pill clutter' the brief bans. 260svh for five one-line tags is slow, and one tag was hidden under the dock in state A. .fh-b duplicates the heading; that is fine because it is aria-hidden, but avoid duplicate visible text. Each concept should show its features in its own terms: hotel services on a night timeline, a clinic instrument panel or checklist, a dental chairside day schedule.

features.name: Live call card: a dot field that ripples with each line
features.what_it_does: (10-y8200.jpg) Below the features is one wide card (7fr / 5fr). The left side is a near-black panel with a 22px dot grid coloured like the sphere, blue rows at the top through orange at the bottom, twinkling. Its header has '● LIVE CALL' (a mint outline pill with a blinking dot), the meta 'ROOM 214 · 11:48 PM' and a running timer '00:01'. A call plays by itself. Typing dots appear first (0.8s for the caller, 1.2s for Amariya), then each bubble. The caller is on the left in an 8% white bubble with a 12% hairline: 'Is the pool open late?' Amariya is on the right in a light bubble with ink text, her words streaming in every 75ms: 'Until 11pm tonight — want me to book you a cabana?' Then the caller: 'Perfect, yes please.' Every line sends a ripple ring through the dots from the speaker's side, pushing them out 6px and making them brighter and larger. The call ends with a mint chip, '✓ Cabana booked for 9 pm', which holds for 3s and lifts away before the next of three calls starts (a late checkout; a booking in Spanish, '¿Tienen una habitación para el viernes?'…). The right side has a 46px phone icon tile that tilts −6° and grows on hover, the title '24/7 call answering', and 'Picks up on the first ring, day or night, holidays included. No hold music, no voicemail, no missed bookings.'
features.how_it_works: .feature-lg is a 7fr/5fr grid with padding 0 and overflow hidden; it becomes one column at ≤960 with the call on top. .call-demo: background #08080a, gap 18, a hairline on its right. canvas.call-field is absolute at z −1 with a 2D context, DPR capped at 2, laid out again on resize. Dots sit every 22px with ±2.5px jitter, coloured by colorFor(height), alpha .16–.42, twinkling at .7 + .3·sin(1.3t + phase). Ripples: band = exp(−(dist − age·280)²/1100)·(1 − age/2.6); each dot moves 6·band, gains .85·glow alpha and grows to 1.6 + 1.8·glow. Each ripple starts 24px in from the speaker's side, or at the centre for the done chip. .call-head: 11px caps, .08em, faint. .call-live: mint border at 35%, background rgba(5,5,6,.7), dot blinking every 1.6s. .call-timer: tabular, margin-left auto. .call-thread: flex column, gap 10, height 262px (300 at ≤600), overflow hidden. .enter runs bubbleIn over .55s, from translateY 12px and scale .94, with the origin at the bottom left or right. .typing dots bounce over 1.2s with .15s/.3s offsets. Each .w fades in over .25s. .out fades the children up 10px over .5s, and the next call starts after .65s. Each line pauses 900ms + 22ms per character. Calls play only while the card is at least 20% visible and the tab is visible (IntersectionObserver threshold .2). Under reduced motion, the first call from the build stays static and the dots draw one still frame. .f-ico: 46px, radius 14, 5% fill, hairline, floated right in the copy; on hover rotate(−6deg) scale(1.06).
features.config_and_data: calls[] per niche, three each, as {meta, done, lines:[['g'|'a', text]]}. Hotels: Room 214 · 11:48 pm → Cabana booked for 9 pm; Room 507 · 7:02 am → Late checkout added; New caller · 9:15 pm (Spanish) → Reserva confirmada · 1 noche. Aesthetics: New client · 8:40 pm → Consultation booked · Sat 11 am; Returning client · 1:15 pm → Moved to Thu 5 pm; New caller · 10:05 pm (Arabic, RTL) → تم حجز الاستشارة · الخميس ٤ م. Dental: New patient · 7:45 am → Urgent visit booked · 3:40 pm; Existing patient · 12:20 pm → Cleaning moved to Tue 10 am; New caller · 6:30 pm (Spanish) → Cita confirmada · lunes 9:00. Also features.card_title and card_desc.
features.port_notes: Keep the scripts for all three niches, including the other languages and RTL via dir=auto. Keep the self-playing call with typing pauses and streamed replies, the outcome chip, and playback only while visible. Upgrade it: the whole card is aria-hidden, so there is no accessible transcript, and it is silent. The research points to 'Hear Amariya take a call', with real audio, a synced transcript and an 'Enable sound' control (Clinic Beethovenstrasse, Sky Clinics). Stage it in each concept's own terms: a hotel night-desk switchboard, a clinic monitor trace, a dental chairside view. Avoid a second generic dot-grid canvas; reuse the concept's own 3D or 2D language.

features.name: Agent spotlight ring (@property conic ring)
features.what_it_does: When the agent highlights a feature (highlight_feature) or recommends a plan, that card lifts 4px (plans 8px), loses its hairline and gains a deep shadow and a slowly rotating 1px rainbow ring (blue → mint → gold → orange) around its edge. Feature icons turn warm, and orbit tags open to show their description.
features.how_it_works: @property --spin <angle> (inherits false). .card.spotlight::before and .plan.recommended::before: absolute, inset −1px (−6px for plans, with radius +6), padding 1px, conic-gradient(from var(--spin), blue, mint, gold, orange, blue), masked to a 1px ring (mask content-box exclude / -webkit-mask-composite xor), animated by spin 6s linear infinite (keyframes to --spin 360deg). .card.spotlight: transform translateY(−4px), transparent border, shadow 0 30px 80px rgba(0,0,0,.5). .feature-lg.spotlight puts the ring at inset 0 because the card clips its overflow. In app.js, spotlightFeature(key) removes .spotlight from every .feature, then adds it to [data-feature=key].
features.config_and_data: highlight_feature keys: answering, bookings, multilingual, guest_requests, upsells, integrations.
features.port_notes: The mechanic is essential: the visitor must see what the voice is pointing at. It must exist in every concept and also be recorded in the transcript's activity log. The rotating rainbow ring is generic, so each concept should point in its own way: the 3D object physically moving to the item or lighting it, a hairline drawing to it, a stamp. Keep the rule of one highlighted item at a time.

features.name: Pricing eclipse: planet horizon, plan cards, recommendation light (content obsolete)
features.what_it_does: (11-y9020.jpg) '04 — PLANS / Plans that fit your property', with 'Simple monthly pricing. Amariya will point out the one that fits you best.' Three equal cards sit over the horizon of a huge dark planet. Starter: 'Up to 40 rooms', $299/month (24/7 call answering, FAQ & guest requests, 5 languages, 500 calls / month). Professional: 'Up to 150 rooms', $799/month, with an outline 'MOST POPULAR' chip (Everything in Starter, Direct bookings via PMS, 30+ languages, Upsells & analytics, 2,500 calls / month). Enterprise: 'Groups & 150+ rooms', 'Custom' (Everything in Professional, Multi-property setup, Custom voice & brand persona, Dedicated success manager, Unlimited calls). Each item has a tick-circle icon, and the list sits under a hairline. The planet's thin rim glows blue → mint → gold → orange across the middle with a soft halo. The planet rises 180px into place and brightens as the section arrives. The cards are lightly frosted, so the rim shows through them softly. When the agent recommends a plan, several things happen. That card turns light (#f3f1ec with ink text), lifts 8px with a deep shadow and the rainbow ring, and shows 'RECOMMENDED FOR YOU' (an ink chip) instead of 'Most popular'. A warm light slides along the rim to sit behind it (0.9s). A centred pill appears below ('Why Professional: …'). And the demo form's plan select is set.
features.how_it_works: .plan-stage: relative, isolation. .eclipse: absolute at z −1, top calc(34% − 150px), bottom −240px, 100vw wide, mask linear(#000 72%, transparent). .planet: top 150px, width max(2400px,210vw), a square circle filled with radial-gradient(closest-side, #050506 96.8%, #0c0c11 99.3%, #16161d 100%), moved by translate3d(−50%, var(--rise), 0). ::before is a ring at inset 0 with 1.5px padding, filled with linear(90deg, transparent 29%, blue 39%, mint 46%, gold 53%, orange 61%, transparent 71%), opacity .55 + .45·--glow. ::after is the same gradient as a ring at inset −46px with 46px padding, blurred 30px, opacity .55·--glow. JS: e = easeOutCubic(clamp((vh − top)/(vh·.9))); --rise = (1−e)·180px; --glow = e. .rim-light: 560×240 at top −110px, left var(--hx), radial(rgba(255,176,104,.55) → rgba(255,140,70,.18) at 55% → transparent), blurred 18px, opacity var(--hl), with transitions of .9s on left and .6s on opacity. A MutationObserver on class changes in .plan-grid, plus resize, sets --hl to 1 and --hx to the recommended card's centre relative to the planet. Cards: .plan has backdrop blur(10px) and padding-top 62px for the badge strip. h3 18px. .pop and .plan-badge sit at top 18, right 18, 11px caps, .08em. .plan-for: 13px muted, margin-bottom 22. .price: 34px Ranade, tabular, with a 13px muted small. The ul has a hairline on top, gap 10, 14px text, and li::before is an 18px tick-circle data URI. .recommended: --light background, --ink text, translateY(−8px), shadow 0 40px 90px .55, muted text rgba(11,11,13,.6), ink ticks. Its .plan-badge appears (from opacity 0 and translateY(−4px), over .35s) and .pop is hidden. .plan-reason: a centred pill, max 760px, surface fill with a hairline, a .5s pop. The grid has three columns with gap 16, one column at ≤960.
features.config_and_data: pricing.title and pricing.plans {starter|professional|enterprise: for, price, offer, items} per niche. Prices were identical on every niche ($299 / $799 / Custom). PLAN_NAMES is in build_pages.py. The JSON-LD SoftwareApplication offers are built from the plans. The agent's recommend_plan({plan, reason}) accepts starter, professional or enterprise.
features.port_notes: The content is obsolete. Replace the three monthly tiers with the decided Founders' offer: a lifetime licence for the first 30 per niche (hotels & restaurants $2,500, clinics $3,500, dental $3,000, provisional); Professional features for life plus 500 call minutes a month (extra at cost); done-for-you setup; one location per licence; the guarantee 'Live in 7 days or your money back'; the honest ledger '30 founding licences · N issued · N held · N open' (no timers, no struck-through prices); and 'after the 30, plans from $299/month'. Keep the mechanic: the agent can recommend or point at an option, and the page lights it and states the reason in words. Remap recommend_plan (e.g. founding licence versus monthly after the 30, or remove it) and the JSON-LD offers. The eclipse rim light is the best CSS lighting on the old site, so match that quality of light. The three-card grid with 'Most popular' and tick lists is stock SaaS and must not return.

features.name: Demo booking: glass circle, drifting lights, form, success (flow obsolete)
features.what_it_does: (11–12) '05 — BOOK A DEMO / Hear Amariya answer your hotel's phone', then 'Tell Amariya your details, or fill them in here. She'll read them back before sending.' and three ticks in a row: 'A 20-minute live call with our team', 'Amariya set up with your hotel's details', 'No commitment, no credit card'. Behind it is an enormous faint glass circle; its 1px rim shows as arcs in the lower corners. Inside are two big blurred lights, blue on the left and mint on the right, which drift slowly and slide in opposite directions as you scroll. The form is a 780px dark-glass card: Your name and Hotel; Email and Phone; Preferred date / time ('e.g. Thursday afternoon') and Plan of interest (Not sure yet / Starter / Professional / Enterprise); Notes; and a full-width light button, 'Request my demo →'. On submit, missing fields show a toast such as 'Please add your name, a valid email address.' On success the form hides and a card pops in with a 64px mint tick, 'You're booked in' and 'Thanks Sam! We'll email sam@… to confirm your demo for Thursday afternoon.' The card takes focus and the page scrolls to it.
features.how_it_works: .demo has padding-bottom 120px. .demo-backdrop: full width, z −1, with 14% mask fades top and bottom. .demo-globe: a min(1680px,150vw) circle, centred, filled with radial(circle at 50% 40%, rgba(255,255,255,.045), .012 at 58%, .03 at 69%, transparent 71%), with a 1px rgba(255,255,255,.1) border and shadows inset 0 2px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.16) and inset 0 0 160px rgba(143,180,255,.07). Each .blob is blurred 80px. Blue: left 5%, top 22%, 34%×46%, radial(rgba(62,127,216,.95) → .35 at 60%), animated drift-a over 22s alternate (rotate −24°→−4°, scale 1→1.12, translate 40,30). Mint: right 7%, bottom 20%, 30%×40%, radial(rgba(134,214,196,.78) → .28 at 60%), animated drift-b over 26s (rotate 18°→−6°, scale 1.05→.95, translate −50,−30). JS also translates them ±p·180px in opposite directions. .demo-head .checks: flex, wrap, centred, gap 10/28 (a column on phones), each li with a 22px tick icon. .demo-form and .demo-success: background rgba(12,12,16,.55) with blur(20px) saturate(1.2). The form has padding 30. The success card has padding 48/28, a .5s pop, and a 64px mint .success-mark. Validation requires a name, a business name and an email matching the regex. Submitting stores the request in localStorage 'aria_demo_requests', logs it with console.info, and optionally POSTs to CONFIG.FORM_WEBHOOK_URL with {fields…, hotel_profile, industry, submitted_at, conversation_id}. The agent's fill_demo_form types into the fields, and submit_demo_request waits for typing to finish.
features.config_and_data: demo.title, demo.check2 and demo.business_label per niche (Hotel / Clinic / Practice…). CONFIG.FORM_WEBHOOK_URL is empty. localStorage key aria_demo_requests. PAGE.industry. The conversation id comes from the SDK.
features.port_notes: The flow is obsolete. Replace 'book a demo' with the two-step Founders' application. Qualified applicants then book a 20-minute call through an embedded HubSpot meetings link, and the invoice follows the call. Submissions must stay pluggable because there are no HubSpot IDs yet. Keep the webhook-or-local fallback, the profile, industry and conversation_id attached to each submission, and the agent tools (fill, read back, submit) remapped to the application's fields. Keep inline validation with human messages, a success state that takes focus, and 'what happens next' ticks, now: application → call → invoice → live in 7 days. Drop the giant glass circle with blurred blue and mint blobs (a banned gradient-blob cliché) and the dark glass form card.

features.name: FAQ accordion
features.what_it_does: (13-y10660.jpg) 'QUESTIONS / What hoteliers ask us', with 'The short answers. Amariya can go into detail if you ask her.' Below are five full-width rounded cards (max 900px). Each is a native disclosure with the question in Ranade 18px on the left and a + icon on the right. Opening one brightens its border, turns the + 135° into an ×, and raises the answer 8px into view (14px muted, max 70ch). The hotels questions: What is an AI receptionist for hotels? / Which languages does Amariya speak? / Does Amariya work with my property management system? / What happens when a guest needs a real person? / How long does setup take?
features.how_it_works: .faq-list: grid, gap 10, max-width 900, centred. Each details.card has padding 0 and joins the reveal stagger. summary: flex space-between, gap 16, min-height 64, padding 18px 24px, list-style none with the marker hidden; h3 18px. .faq-ico: 22px with a .45s transform. [open]: --line-strong border and the icon at rotate(135deg). p: padding 0 24px 22px, with a .5s rise animation. There is no backdrop (the old README: 'FAQ: plain'); the global field shows faintly at 40%.
features.config_and_data: faq.title and faq.items[{q, a}] per niche, five each. Aesthetics adds 'Will Amariya give medical advice?' and 'How do deposits work?'. Dental adds 'How does Amariya handle urgent calls?' and 'Can she book new and existing patients?'.
features.port_notes: Keep native details and summary (they work with the keyboard and without JS) and the per-niche questions. Add the objections the research flags: 'Isn't this just another AI chatbot?'; the price question ('why a one-time licence', 'why this price'); privacy, recording and data handling (GDPR, plus HIPAA-style handling for clinics); 'what if she gets it wrong'; and 'what happens after the 30'. An h3 inside summary works but some screen readers announce it oddly, so test it. Visually, a stack of identical rounded cards is a template accordion. Re-imagine it per concept (episodes, tabs by topic, a filterable index), and let 'Ask Amariya' answer any question by voice.

features.name: Footer: closing CTA, giant outline wordmark, the orb returns
features.what_it_does: (14-y11480.jpg) A full-screen close. 'Your front desk, never off duty.' is centred, with the second line in grey, above a light 'Talk to Amariya' pill with a mic. Under it the name 'Amariya' is a giant outline (1px stroke at 18% white, tight −.06em tracking) spanning the full content width and drifting ±45px with scroll. The particle sphere returns at full brightness, centred on the wordmark, with a warm orange glow behind the call to action. The last row sits under a hairline: the ring logo and 'Amariya' (muted) on the left, '© 2026 Amariya AI · Voice powered by ElevenLabs' on the right (13px faint).
features.how_it_works: .footer: min-height 100svh, flex column justify-end, padding 0 gutter 120px (110 at ≤600), margin-top 140px, overflow hidden, isolation. --glow is radial(22% 22% at 50% 40%, rgba(255,150,70,.3)) plus radial(46% 40% at 50% 46%, rgba(242,140,80,.12)), painted on ::before (140vw wide, moved by --gy). .footer-cta: z1, column, centred, gap 28; h2 max 15ch. .wordmark: --wordmark-em 4.05; font 400 min(30rem, (100vw − 2·clamp(16px,4vw,48px))/4.05)/.78 Ranade; letter-spacing −.06em; transparent fill with -webkit-text-stroke 1px rgba(255,255,255,.18); margin 56px 0 .2em to leave room for the descender; pointer-events none; transform translate3d(0, var(--py), 0). .footer-meta: flex space-between, wrap, hairline on top, padding-top and margin-top 28, max 1240, 13px faint; .logo is muted. app.js fills [data-year].
features.config_and_data: footer.title is the same on every niche: 'Your front desk, never off duty.'. Company 'Amariya AI' (site.json). The ElevenLabs credit.
features.port_notes: Keep a final talk CTA, the agent's body returning as a bookend, the automatic year, the company line and the 'Voice powered by ElevenLabs' credit. Add the legal links the old site lacked: privacy, terms and a recording notice. A full-width outline wordmark is now a common award-site trope, and the dock covered its bottom in the screenshot. Re-imagine the close per concept: a hotel night turning to dawn, a sign-off on a clinic chart, a dental appointment card. The wordmark face is Ranade under the new rules.

features.name: Conversation dock: states, captions, level bars, live actions
features.what_it_does: (Visible in every screenshot.) A bar is fixed at the bottom centre: 540px wide, rounded 26px, dark translucent glass with a hairline and a large soft shadow. On the left is a 44px particle mini orb button, which swells up to 8% with the voice level. Next to it are a status line in small tracked caps ('AMARIYA IS READY TO TALK') and a caption ('Press the orb and say hello.'). States: Connecting shows 'Connecting', with the caption 'Allow microphone access to talk with Amariya…' or 'Opening the chat…'. Thinking shows 'Thinking' plus three animated dots, with the caption 'Amariya is joining…'. Listening shows 'Listening' in mint with five level bars; it reads 'Mic muted' when muted and 'Your turn' in text mode. Speaking shows 'Amariya is speaking' with the level bars. The dock's border turns mint while listening and warm while speaking. Captions cross-fade to the latest line: Amariya's in white, the visitor's as 'You: …' in mint. After a call the caption reads 'Thanks for chatting — tap the orb to pick it back up.' Buttons appear on the right only while live: show conversation; mute, which turns red and swaps to a mic-off icon; and end call, which turns red on hover. Opening the conversation expands the dock; at 900px and up it moves to the right edge, 400px wide. Escape closes the conversation.
features.how_it_works: .dock: fixed, left 50%, bottom calc(16px + safe-area), translateX(−50%), z30; width min(540px, 100% − 32px); background rgba(14,14,17,.74) with backdrop blur(20px) saturate(1.3); 1px --line; radius 26; shadow 0 20px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.5); width transitions over .45s and border over .4s. [data-state=speaking] sets the border to rgba(242,167,126,.5), and listening to rgba(134,214,196,.5). .dock-bar: flex, gap 12, padding 9/10/9/11. .dock-status: 11px, .12em caps, weight 600, rgba(243,241,236,.6); mint while listening, 70% white while speaking. While thinking, its ::after is an 18×6 strip of dots revealed by clip-path in steps(4) over 1s. .wave: five 3px-wide bars, each 3px + --level·11px·k tall (k = .5/.85/1/.7/.4), shown only while listening or speaking in voice mode. .dock-caption: 13px, nowrap, ellipsis, with a title attribute holding the full text; .swap sets opacity 0 for the 120ms swap, and .user is mint. At ≥900px, .expanded sets right 24px, width 400px and transform none. At ≤600px the dock is calc(100% − 16px) wide at bottom 8px + safe area, with radius 22. app.js setState(state) writes dock[data-state], dock[data-mode] and body[data-state], sets the status text and the orb label text, hides [data-live-only] while idle or connecting, and hides #muteBtn in text mode. Level loop: the target is getOutputVolume() while speaking, getInputVolume() while listening and unmuted, else 0. smooth += (min(1, level·2.2) − smooth)·.35 each frame, and the result is written as --level on every [data-orb] and on .wave. Tone: ElevenLabs v3 tags in the agent's text ([excited], [softly], [reassuring], [warmly]…) set [data-tone] on the dock and body. On connect a chime plays: two sine notes, 660 Hz then 880 Hz.
features.config_and_data: STATUS: idle 'Amariya is ready to talk', connecting 'Connecting', listening 'Listening', thinking 'Thinking', speaking 'Amariya is speaking'; plus 'Mic muted' and 'Your turn'. TONES: excited, playfully, laughs softly → bright; softly, sighs, thoughtful → soft; reassuring → calm; warmly, curious → warm (warm is the default). CONFIG.AGENT_ID (agent_9101m3n1hwxffey830jzf43chj6x), with a per-page PAGE.agentId override, and PAGE.agentContext. Visit context: time_of_day, visitor_status (new or returning), visitor_device; TTS speed set by time of day with ±.02 jitter, stability .3 ±.04.
features.port_notes: Every behaviour must survive: five states, text and voice modes, mute, tone, live level from both input and output, captions that distinguish the speaker, buttons shown only while live, Escape, the chime, falling back to text when the mic is denied, and the caption after a call ends. There is an accessibility gap to fix: the dock status is not a live region (only the transcript is). The brief requires the orb status in a live region; the new Orb.astro has one, but only for listening and speaking. There is a visual gap too. The bar is a generic glass 'AI assistant' pill that covered content on every screen (the last FAQ row, the demo lede, the footer wordmark), and it forced a hero workaround at 1101–1447px. The old MASTER.md checklist even says 'Content not hidden behind the fixed dock'. Each concept should make the persistent conversation UI part of its world (for example, the 3D character docks and becomes the control), and reserve space or step aside when forms or the footer are on screen.

features.name: Transcript panel, messages and composer
features.what_it_does: Inside the expanded dock, above the bar, are a header 'CONVERSATION' with a collapse chevron, a scrolling thread and a composer. Amariya's messages sit on the left in an 8% white bubble, and the visitor's on the right in a light bubble with ink text, both with 5px tail corners. Agent actions appear as small centred lines with a dot: 'Updated your hotel profile', 'Calculated your estimate', 'Recommended the professional plan', 'Filled in your demo details', 'Demo request sent'. While she thinks, a typing bubble shows three bouncing dots. The composer is a pill input, 'Type a message…', with a light 38px send button.
features.how_it_works: .panel has a hairline at the bottom and enters with panelIn over .4s. .panel-head: flex, padding 12/12/4/18, 11px caps, .12em, weight 600, 55%. ol.thread: list-style none, padding 8/14/12, max-height min(46vh,380px) (42vh at ≤600), overflow auto, flex column with gap 8, overscroll contained, data-lenis-prevent, aria-live polite. .msg: max 85%, padding 9/13, radius 16, 14px, entering with msgIn over .35s. .msg.activity: centred, 13px, 70%, with a 5px dot. .msg.typing: 6px dots bouncing over 1.2s, with aria-label 'Amariya is thinking'. .composer: flex, gap 8, padding 0 10 10; the input is a pill with padding .6em 1em at 16px. Typing in the composer calls sendUserActivity(). Submitting calls sendUserMessage, shows the visitor's bubble, sets the caption to 'You: …' and the state to thinking.
features.config_and_data: Activity strings are in the app.js client tools and use PAGE.businessNoun. Audio tags are stripped from displayed text by clean().
features.port_notes: Keep text chat as capable as voice, and keep the activity log: it is the accessible record of what the agent did to the page. Restyle it per concept. Keep data-lenis-prevent (or an equivalent) so the thread scrolls inside smooth scrolling. Raise the 32px collapse and 38px send targets to 44px.

features.name: Start sheet: setting expectations before the mic prompt
features.what_it_does: The first time a visitor starts voice, a centred modal appears before the browser's mic prompt. It shows a 64px particle orb, 'Say hello to Amariya', and three bullets with bold leads. 'A quick chat, about 3 minutes.' is followed by 'She'll ask about your hotel and walk you through the site as you talk.' 'Uses your microphone.' is followed by 'Your browser will ask for permission. You can mute or switch to typing any time.' The third reads 'Interrupt her whenever you like, just like a normal conversation.' Below are 'Start with voice' (light, focused) and 'Type instead' (ghost), plus a close × that spins 90° on hover. The page behind dims to 60% black with a 6px blur.
features.how_it_works: A <dialog> opened with showModal(), holding a form with method=dialog, so returnValue is voice, text or cancel. sheetSeen means it shows once per page load; later voice starts skip it, and text starts never show it. .sheet: background #0e0e12, 1px hairline, radius 26, padding 34/30/28, width min(460px, 100% − 32px), shadow 0 40px 100px .7. [open] runs sheetIn over .45s (from translateY 16px and scale .98). ::backdrop is rgba(0,0,0,.6) with blur(6px). .sheet-close is 44px at top and right 12px, and rotates 90deg on hover. The sheet's mini orb animates only while the sheet is open.
features.config_and_data: sheet.ask per niche ('She'll ask about your hotel…'). If AGENT_ID is missing, a toast says so instead.
features.port_notes: Keep the step that sets expectations before the permission prompt (it builds trust and respects privacy), its per-niche copy, native dialog semantics, autofocus on the voice option and the returnValue flow. Add what the research suggests: a mic test or level check (GetLayers Orb Studio), and a privacy line for clinics. Style it per concept.

features.name: Follow pill (polite agent navigation) and toast
features.what_it_does: Follow pill: the page does not jump if the agent wants to move it while the visitor is reading, meaning any wheel, touch, key or pointer input in the last 2.5s. Instead a light pill appears above the dock, 'Amariya is showing plans ↓'; clicking it scrolls there, and it disappears if the visitor arrives on their own. Toast: a small light pill slides down at the top centre for 2.8s with system messages: 'Add your ElevenLabs agent ID in config.js to enable voice.', 'Connection hiccup — please try again.', 'No microphone access — switching to text chat.', 'Couldn't start the conversation. Please try again.', 'Please add your name, email.'
features.how_it_works: .follow-pill: fixed at bottom calc(92px + safe-area), centred, z29, min-height 44, padding 9/16, light fill with ink text, 13px weight 500, shadow 0 10px 30px .4, entering with pillIn over .35s. Its label comes from SECTION_LABELS. Agent scrolling uses easeInOutCubic over clamp(|dist|·.45, 500, 1100)ms, is cancelled by any visitor input, updates the URL with history.replaceState #section, and is instant under reduced motion. Input inside #dock, .sheet or .follow-pill does not count as reading. .toast: fixed at top 24, centred, z40, a light 13px pill moving from translate(−50%,−20px) to 0 with opacity over .3s, role=status.
features.config_and_data: SECTION_LABELS: the intro / PAGE.sectionLabel / features / plans / demo booking. Reading window 2,500ms. After an agent scroll, 1,800ms pass before the visitor's own navigation is reported to the agent as a contextual update.
features.port_notes: Keep this exactly. Polite agent navigation that never hijacks the page is a real differentiator, and the visitor's own navigation is reported back to the agent. In the new build, agent navigation must also cooperate with Lenis and with each concept's pinned scenes: it should scroll to a scene's state, not just to the top of a section. Toast copy should take each niche's voice, and configuration errors must never reach real visitors.

features.name: Mini particle orbs, tone filters, no-WebGL fallback
features.what_it_does: Besides the main field there are three small particle spheres: one in the ROI card corner (200px, decorative, slow), one in the dock button (44px) and one in the start sheet (64px). The last two react to voice level and state like the big one. While Amariya speaks, the small orbs shift with the emotion of her line: brighter and more saturated (excited), softer and dimmer (softly, thoughtful), slightly cooler (reassuring). Without WebGL, every orb, including the hero, becomes a quiet ring in the orb colours on black, and the background field disappears.
features.how_it_works: .orb: radius 50%, overflow hidden, --bg fill, transitions of .08s linear on transform and .8s on filter; its canvas sits at inset 0. Point counts: ROI 2,200 (still: ignores voice and state), dock 1,400, sheet 2,400. Rotation increases by dt·(.25 + level·.8 + thinking·.6). Each is drawn only when its host has client rects and is on screen, with tilt .3, point size 1.15 and scale .8. .orb-sm: 44px with a 1px ring and scale(1 + level·.08). .orb-xs: 64px. Tone filters while speaking: [data-tone=bright] saturate(1.3) brightness(1.1); soft saturate(.75) brightness(.92); calm hue-rotate(−14deg) saturate(.9). html.no-webgl gives .orb-anchor and .orb the background radial-gradient(circle, var(--bg) 60%, transparent 62%), var(--orb-ring) at opacity .9, and sets .fx to display none. A page can hold up to four separate WebGL contexts.
features.config_and_data: Counts and speeds are in experience.js; tones come from app.js TONES.
features.port_notes: Keep: the agent's body appearing wherever the conversation lives (dock, sheet), tone tinting, voice reactivity, and a designed still image when WebGL is missing (the new project already has CSS stills per orb, which is good). Change: avoid several WebGL contexts; use one renderer with scissor viewports, or DOM stills at small sizes. The ROI corner orb, clipped by its card, looked like an accident. The new boot.ts mounts only the first [data-orb] and requires WebGL2, so devices with only WebGL1 must get the fallback gracefully.

features.name: Responsive behaviour (all breakpoints)
features.what_it_does: Desktop was the designed view; phones kept every function. At ≤1100px the hero becomes a column: orb on top with the title still inside it, then the intro and buttons at full width. At ≤960 the profile and ROI cards, the call card and the plans stack into one column. At ≤761 the features become a plain grid with no pin. At ≤600 the industry links move under the brand, the scroll cue hides, the story shortens, form rows stack and the dock spans the width. At ≤734 the two hero buttons share one row.
features.how_it_works: 1101–1447: .hero-foot moves to bottom 104px to clear the dock. ≥900: .dock.expanded sits at right 24px, 400px wide. ≤1100: .hero{--orb:min(62vw,520px); --pt:104px; flex column; padding var(--pt) 20px 64px; min-height 0}; .hero-orb is relative; .hero-title sits at top calc(pt + orb/2); .hero-foot is relative with margin-top 88, max 560, column, gap 28. ≤1068 and ≤734: the type steps listed under tokens. ≤960: .profile-grid is 1fr; .section-head gap 12; .feature-lg is 1fr (call on top, hairline below); .plan-grid is 1fr. ≤761 (JS matchMedia min-width 761px): .orbit-live is off. Under 760 (JS): field radius ×1.15 and alpha ×.8. Under 700 (JS): 11,000 points. ≤600: .hero{--orb:min(86vw,360px); --pt:118px}; .brand top 22; .industry-nav at top 62, centred, links 6px 10px; .call-thread 300px; .scroll-cue none; .story 340svh; .beat padding-bottom 20svh; .row2 1fr; demo checks in a column; .section padding-top 96; profile light at top 106; .dock width calc(100% − 16px) at bottom 8px, radius 22; .thread 42vh; ROI orb 150px; footer padding-bottom 110. ≤734: .hero-actions nowrap with gap 8; buttons flex 1 1 auto with padding-inline .9em. Coarse pointers get no Lenis (native scrolling), and the card cursor light runs only under (hover: hover). Inputs are 16px, so iOS does not zoom. The dock and follow pill respect safe-area insets. The hero, story and pins use svh units.
features.config_and_data: Breakpoints are hard-coded; nothing differs per niche.
features.port_notes: The old phone layout was the desktop stacked. It had no moments designed for phones: the features lost their pin, and the story simply got shorter. Each new concept must design its phone version as a full composition in its own right: a conversation control within thumb reach, an orb you can move by touch drag, and pinned scenes that work with native touch scrolling. Keep svh units, safe-area insets, 16px inputs, no smooth-scroll takeover on touch, and tiered 3D detail. The new project's breakpoints are 1068/900/734; unify them per concept. Known old risks: the industry bar was close to overflowing at 320px, and the dock covered about 64px of every phone screen.

features.name: Reduced motion and no-JS behaviour
features.what_it_does: With reduced motion the page is static but complete. There are no letter or word animations and no entrance blur, and the marquee stops. The story unpins into three stacked centred lines, with no clock, greetings or counter. The features show as a grid. The eclipse and demo lights are still. The call card shows its first conversation. The particle field and mini orbs are drawn as still frames that update only on scroll, resize or when the dialog opens. Count-ups, agent typing and agent scrolling are instant. Without JavaScript the story beats and the features grid render as static content; voice, chat, ROI and form submission need JS.
features.how_it_works: CSS @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): html scroll-behavior auto; .reveal visible; all animations set to .01ms × 1; .marquee-track none; .js .story height auto; .story-pin relative; .beat relative, opacity 1, centred, padding 80px 24px; .beat-time, .greetings and .story-count hidden. JS: experience.js and app.js read reducedMotion from matchMedia once at load (not live). When it is set they skip splitText, scrubs, risers, glows, the profile light, the call loop and Lenis. stillFrames() redraws at time 2 on resize, scroll and sheet open, and setStageLive is false. Without JS, html has no .js class, so .story and .beat use the unpinned rules (lines 167-169). The forms have no action attribute, so submitting needs JS.
features.config_and_data: none
features.port_notes: Keep the principle 'static but complete' and extend it. The brief adds a visible Pause motion control that must pause every animation on the page, not only the orb. The new hero has one; the old site had none. Listen for live changes to the media query: the old code read it once, and the new OrbStage listens, which is good. Still frames must still show state changes, as the new stage.still() does. The application form must work without JS (progressive enhancement with a real action or endpoint), because it is the conversion path.

features.name: Current Astro hero previews: the shared shell
features.what_it_does: (orb-*-1440-*.jpg, orb-*-390-idle.jpg) There are three hero-only pages, built from one template. The nav has 'Amariya' (Ranade 500, 23px) on the left, a centred segmented industry switcher 'Hotels & restaurants | Clinics | Dental' (the current item filled with the raised surface colour), and an outlined 'Apply' pill on the right. The hero has: an eyebrow 'AI RECEPTIONIST FOR …' (12px, .16em, accent); a serif H1, 'A front desk that never misses a call / consultation / patient.', with 'never' in the accent colour; a lede; a facts row with hairline dividers (clinics and dental only); two buttons, a filled 'Apply for a founding licence' and an outlined 'Talk to Amariya' or 'Hear Amariya' with a mic icon; an offer line, e.g. 'Founding licence $3,500 once, for the first 30 clinics', with a ledger chip '• 30 of 30 open'; the guarantee 'Live in 7 days or your money back.'; and a text button 'Pause motion' at the bottom right, which toggles to 'Play motion'. Layout is the only structural difference: hotels is centred with the orb above the text, clinics is split with text left and orb right, and dental is split the other way with the orb on the left. On a 390px phone the nav wraps: brand and Apply on row 1, and the switcher full width with three equal segments on row 2. The orb is on top, and the primary button is full width. Hotels also has a 6% fractal-noise film grain over the page.
features.how_it_works: global.css: tokens come from [data-theme] (hospitality dark, clinics light, dental light). features.name: Current Astro hero previews: the three orbs, their states and today's pointer response
features.what_it_does: Hotels, champagne liquid glass (orb-hotels-1440-idle/listening/speaking.jpg): a thick glass sphere about 360px across with sharp white speculars and a warm halo, holding a cloudy amber-khaki nebula. Listening: the rim wobbles slightly and the core warms. Speaking: the surface deforms strongly into a lumpy liquid blob with caustic highlights and brighter gold. Clinics, frosted porcelain (orb-clinics-1440-*): a matte white sphere inside four corner brackets, with a soft steel-blue blot glowing inside and a pale blue halo. A 1.5px steel line crosses it like a monitor trace: flat when idle, a gentle two-hump wave when listening, tall peaks when speaking, while the blot spreads and the halo strengthens. Dental, rosé pearl (orb-dental-1440-*): a white pearl with faint rainbow fringes and small coloured speculars, floating over a soft elliptical contact shadow. Listening and speaking barely change it; it is slightly larger when speaking.
features.how_it_works: OrbStage (stage.ts) uses a WebGLRenderer (antialias, alpha set per scene) with DPR capped at 1.5 (1.25 on coarse pointers). States idle, listening and speaking blend with a 90ms time constant. Amp rises in about 40ms and falls in about 200ms, and applies only while speaking (ampSource). The pointer is the cursor relative to the orb's box (−1.5 to 1.5), eased over 250ms. An IntersectionObserver (120px margin), visibilitychange, reduced motion and Pause all switch to a single still frame that still shows the state. If more than 60% of 90 frames exceed 20ms after a 1.5s warm-up, it degrades once (DPR 1 and lighter effects). On WebGL context loss it pauses and removes .is-live. boot.ts requires WebGL2, lazy-loads the niche's scene and sets window.amariyaOrb. It wires Pause ('Pause motion' / 'Play motion', aria-pressed) and a preview talk button that runs listening for 1.8s, speaking until 7.6s, then idle, with a speech-like amp of about 5 syllables a second. Today's pointer response: champagne sets rotation.y = .08t + .2·x and rotation.x = −.14·y (champagne.ts 202-203). Porcelain's frost clears under the cursor, but only while listening (porcelain.ts 57). Pearl dimples toward the cursor, but only while listening (pearl.ts 84, 133-134). There is no drag, no inertia, no touch manipulation and no keyboard control.
features.config_and_data: Orb colour roles per theme. Hospitality: orb-glass, highlight, tint, core-deep, core, core-hot, dust, glow. Clinics: orb-body, shade, glow-deep, glow, glow-hot, line. Dental: orb-highlight, body, sheen, sheen-listen, edge, shadow (tokens.css).
features.port_notes: Request 1 ('make orb moveable with mouse, 3D') is not met yet: the pointer only nudges rotation or acts while listening. Each concept needs direct 3D manipulation: grab and rotate with inertia and spring-back, a response as the cursor comes near, touch drag on phones, arrow keys when focused, and a still under reduced motion. It also needs the missing states (connecting, thinking), tone, and reaction to the listening level. On materials: champagne is the most convincing in 3D, but its idle core reads as muddy khaki and as a 'crystal ball'. Porcelain's blot reads as an iris or a bruise, and its idle line is nearly invisible. Pearl reads as a plain white ball with a dark aliased rim on its lower-right edge, and its states are almost identical. State must be obvious in still images and for colour-blind visitors, so carry it in shape and motion, not hue alone.

features.name: Critique A: what felt premium in the previous design (keep the ideas, not the look)
features.what_it_does: (1) One character across the whole scroll. The particle sphere becomes a voice waveform, then a starfield, anchors the estimate, holds the centre of the features, and returns on the wordmark. Few sites have a through-line that coherent. (2) A live, personal moment. The story opens at the visitor's own time (an outline clock, a blinking colon, 12/24h) with day or night copy, and greetings in nine languages leave the orb, showing the multilingual claim instead of stating it. (3) The voice agent drives the page. It scrolls politely (the follow pill instead of a hijack), types into the form character by character with a warm ring and flash, counts up the ROI, spotlights features, recommends a plan with a sliding rim light and a stated reason, and fills and submits the booking. That is the strongest product demonstration possible. (4) The live call card: calls that play themselves, with typing pauses, streamed replies, ripples through a dot field from the speaker's side, an outcome chip, and real multilingual and RTL scripts. (5) Refined light. The eclipse planet has a rim, an atmosphere and a rim light; the frosted half globe has a warm light that spreads. Both are careful, layered CSS lighting with clipping and masks. (6) Text that resolves like a live transcript (letters unblurring in random order). It suits a voice product and stays accessible through sr-only twins. (7) Craft details: tabular numerals; a wordmark sized to always fit; the story counter; the scroll cue; orbs tinted by tone from ElevenLabs audio tags; the connect chime; greetings and TTS pacing that adapt to the visit; a start sheet that sets expectations before the mic prompt; falling back to text when the mic is denied; still frames under reduced motion.
features.how_it_works: Screenshots 00-y0, 01-y820, 03-y2460, 06-y4920, 10-y8200 and 11-y9020 show these at their best. The code is listed in the entries above (experience.js scenes, story, call, eclipse and profile light; app.js client tools, typing, follow pill and visit context).
features.config_and_data: Per-niche scripts, greetings, ROI assumptions, story lines and day/night copy (industries/*.json, page.greetings, page.roi).
features.port_notes: These are the old site's assets. Carry every one of them into all three concepts, each in that niche's own form. None of the old visual skin is needed to deliver them.

features.name: Critique B: what felt dated or 'AI-generated' (do not port)
features.what_it_does: (1) Palette: black with blue, mint, gold and orange aurora gradients is the default 'AI startup' look. It was identical on hotels, aesthetics and dental, so there was no niche identity at all. (2) Glassmorphism everywhere: the industry bar, the feature capsules, the dock, the plan cards, the demo form, the frosted dome and the giant glass circle are all glass. This is the banned 'glass pill clutter'. (3) Glass capsules orbiting a glowing sphere in the features section is a Dribbble and mdx.so trope, and one capsule sat hidden under the dock. (4) Gradient blobs: the amber blob in the profile section and the drifting blue and mint blobs in the demo are a banned cliché. (5) SaaS rhythm: every section is a centred numbered eyebrow, a half-grey 29px h2, a muted lede and cards. Add three-tier pricing with 'Most popular' and tick lists, a 'Book a demo' form, an FAQ of identical rounded cards and a 'Built for' marquee. (6) The half-grey headline trick (em at 70% white) runs on every heading, including the hero. It gives the template away, and the new previews repeat it as an accent 'never' on all three niches. (7) The particles: about 26,000 dim, dusty points look like a stock three.js example and are too faint to light a hero; halfway through the wave morph the sphere looks like a squashed disc. (8) Pacing: long stretches of dead scroll. The story is 420svh for three lines and the features 260svh for five tags, with empty bands in screenshots 04, 05, 10 and 11. It feels sparse, not deliberate. (9) The persistent dock covers content on every screen (the last FAQ row, the demo lede, the footer wordmark, a feature tag) and forced a hero workaround; it reads as a generic 'AI assistant bar'. (10) Redundant CTAs: five ways to start the same conversation in the first viewport. (11) Contrast: headings stay invisible until the observer fires, so sections appear blank on fast scroll. Unlit scrub text at 20% white measures about 1.6:1 and 35% placeholders about 3:1, both failing AA. Faint 50% text measures about 4.8:1 only on pure black and drops over the warm and blue lights. (12) Type: small and uniform, with h2 at 29px and one face for every role, so the hero and the sections have no typographic contrast. (13) Accidents: the ROI mini orb is clipped in the card corner, and the '—' stats before any input look broken.
features.how_it_works: Evidence: screenshots 04-y3280 (empty starfield), 05-y4100 (empty band above the marquee), 07-y5740 (only 4 of 5 tags visible), 10-y8200 (heading missing, 300px gap), 11-y9020 (three-tier SaaS cards), 12-y9840 (blobs and glass form), 13-y10660 (template accordion with the dock over the last row), 14-y11480 (dock over the wordmark). The styles.css lines are in the entries above. Contrast was computed with the WCAG relative-luminance formula over #050506 and the input fill.

features.port_notes: None of these visual patterns should appear in any of the three new concepts. Where a function lived inside one of them (the dock, the pricing cards, the demo form, the FAQ), keep the function and give it a form native to its concept.

features.name: Critique C: the current Astro hero previews
features.what_it_does: Good: the palettes are tasteful and AA-measured. The display faces are well chosen and tuned per face (Cormorant Garamond for hotels, Newsreader Light for clinics, Instrument Serif for dental). The founding offer, the honest ledger chip and the guarantee are visible above the fold on clinics and dental. Pause motion and the orb's live region exist, and hotels has a film grain. Clinics' brackets with a trace line are the most original idea and the truest to its niche (Neko-like); champagne is the most physical material. Weak: (1) It is one template recoloured: the same shell, the same headline formula with an accent 'never', the same pair of pill CTAs and the same offer row. Only the column order (centre, split, split reversed) and the palette and face differ, which is exactly what the latest request rejects. (2) Hotels uses the stock centred AI-landing stack (orb, eyebrow, H1, lede, two buttons). Its idle orb looks like a muddy khaki crystal ball with a plain radial glow, and the offer, guarantee and Pause sit below the fold at 1440×900. (3) In clinics, the diffuse blue blot inside the white sphere reads as an iris or a bruise, and the idle trace is nearly invisible. (4) Dental's pearl reads as a plain white ball; its iridescence is too faint, its three states look nearly the same in stills, and its lower-right silhouette has a dark aliased edge. At 390px the facts row wraps with a stray divider. (5) The orbs only nudge or react under the cursor while listening; they cannot be moved. (6) Everything below the hero is still missing: story, profile and ROI, features, live call, offer, application, FAQ, footer, dock, sheet, transcript, follow pill and toast. There is also no sound and no character that persists through the scroll.
features.how_it_works: Seen in the 12 preview images and confirmed in global.css, Hero.astro, Nav.astro, niches.ts and the orb scripts listed above.
features.config_and_data: niches.ts layout values center / split / split-reverse are currently the only structural variation.
features.port_notes: Treat the previews as a material study and token base, not as the hero design. Each concept should change the object's role, not only its material: what the 3D thing is and does in that niche's story, where it lives, how you handle it. The navigation and the hero composition must differ per concept.

features.name: The bar the three new concepts must surpass (acceptance checklist)
features.what_it_does: (1) Distinctness: shown as three thumbnails side by side, with logos and colours removed, the concepts must still be clearly different sites. Each needs its own page architecture, navigation and scroll paradigm, layout grid, motion language, type system and signature 3D. (2) Continuity: each has one persistent 3D character, at least as continuous as the old particle field's six scenes, that is also the agent's body in every state (idle, connecting, listening, thinking, speaking, plus tone and level for both input and output). (3) Movable in 3D: grab and rotate with inertia, a response as the cursor comes near, touch drag, keyboard control when focused, a still under reduced motion, and a clear focus ring; that state stays readable without relying on colour. (4) Nothing lost: the local-time story with the day/night swap; multilingual greetings including RTL; the profile with live ROI and agent typing, flash and count-up; feature spotlight; a self-playing call demo (now audible, with a transcript); polite agent navigation with the follow pill and self-navigation reported back; text chat with the activity log; the start sheet; toasts; the five-state dock behaviours; and every client tool remapped to the founders' application. (5) The new commercial core: the Founders' offer, ledger and guarantee above the fold on every niche; the two-step application leading to an embedded HubSpot meeting, then an invoice; submissions kept pluggable. (6) Lighting at least as refined as the eclipse rim and frosted dome, with no glass pills, gradient blobs, aurora-on-black or centred SaaS section rhythm. (7) Pacing: no dead stretches of scroll. Every pinned scene changes something visibly at every 10% of its progress, and the story completes in about half the old scroll length. (8) Accessibility: text at AA on the rendered pixels in every animated state; a live region for agent status; a Pause motion control that stops everything; 44px targets; content never hidden under the persistent conversation UI. (9) Performance: one WebGL context per page where possible; DPR caps; detail tiers; offscreen and hidden-tab pausing; a one-time degrade; Three.js loaded when idle; a designed still when WebGL is missing; no per-frame layout thrash (the old page read getBoundingClientRect in more than 10 updaters every frame).
