features.port_notes: Use this as the judge's acceptance gate for each concept spec and each built page.

cross_cutting: ACCESSIBILITY, previous site. What it got right: a skip link to #profile; sr-only twins for every split or animated text, with the visual layer aria-hidden; all decoration aria-hidden (canvases, clock, greetings, marquee track, backdrops, call card); the transcript thread is aria-live polite and the toast role=status; dialog semantics with returnValue and autofocus; aria-pressed on mute, aria-expanded on the transcript button, aria-current on the industry links; 2px white focus-visible at offset 3 (inputs use a border plus a 4px ring); targets at least 44px except the 40px icon buttons, 32px collapse and 38px send; inputs at 16px; native details and summary for the FAQ; tabular numerals. Gaps to fix. The dock status is not a live region, so voice state changes go unannounced. The hero orb's focus ring is a faint 1px dashed line at 50% white. The live call card is entirely aria-hidden with no accessible transcript. Unlit scrub text at 20% measures about 1.6:1. Placeholders at 35% measure about 3:1. Faint 50% text measures about 4.8:1 only on pure #050506 and drops over the amber and blue lights. Headings stay invisible until an observer fires. The dock covers content. REDUCED MOTION and NO-JS: a full CSS block plus JS gating. The old JS read the media query once at load; the new OrbStage listens for changes. Everything degrades to static but complete content; the story unpins into three lines; the features become a grid; WebGL draws still frames on scroll and resize. No Pause motion control existed before; the brief requires one that pauses everything, not only the orb. The forms have no action attribute, so submitting needs JS; make the application progressively enhanced. PERFORMANCE PATTERNS: particles boot on requestIdleCallback; DPR capped at 2 (the new stage uses 1.5, or 1.25 on coarse pointers); 26,000 points on desktop and 11,000 under 700px; mini orbs drawn only when on screen or the dialog is open; the call canvas runs only when at least 20% visible and the tab is visible. Risks not to repeat: the main rAF loop never stopped; more than 10 updaters called getBoundingClientRect every frame; up to four WebGL contexts; large backdrop-filter layers (dock, tags, plans, form, dome) plus an animated blur(80px) on the blobs and a per-letter filter blur; Lenis and the ElevenLabs client loaded from the jsDelivr CDN (lenis@1.3.26, @elevenlabs/client@1.25.0), which the new project should bundle from npm. The new stage already adds IntersectionObserver and visibility pausing, a one-time degrade and context-loss handling. TEST HOOKS: window.ariaTools (every client tool can be called from the console); localStorage keys aria_demo_requests and aria_visited; console.info('Demo request:'); window.amariyaOrb in the new project (setState, setAmpSource, setPaused); data-* hooks listed per feature; html.js and html.no-webgl flags; body[data-state] and body[data-tone] for visual tests. ERROR HANDLING: WebGL or shader failure is caught and sets html.no-webgl with a ring fallback; a failed mini orb removes its canvas; a failed Lenis import logs a warning; an SDK import or session error shows a toast and resets the UI; a mic NotAllowedError switches to text mode with a toast; webhook failure logs to console.error but still shows success locally; parsing of the call-scripts JSON is guarded; localStorage access is wrapped in try/catch; a missing AGENT_ID shows a toast. PORT RULES from the old README: keep every ID, data-* attribute and form field name that app.js and the agent's client tools use (field names stay hotel_* on every niche; only labels change), or remap the agent's tool definitions in the same change. NON-VISUAL HEAD to preserve per page: title, description, canonical, OG and Twitter cards with og-image.png at 1200×630, favicon SVG and PNG, apple-touch-icon, manifest, theme-color, and JSON-LD (Organization, WebSite, SoftwareApplication with offers, Service); the offers must change to the Founders' licence. Sitemap and robots were generated by build_pages.py.
